Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the midpoint of the line segment joining each pair of points (a)–(k).
The line segment $$AB$$ has endpoints $$A(-2,5)$$ and $$B(a,b).$$ The midpoint of $$AB$$ is $$M(4,3).$$ Find the values of $$a$$ and $$b.$$
The line segment $$PQ$$ is a diameter of a circle, where $$P(-4,6),Q(7,8).$$ Find the coordinates of the centre of the circle.
The line segment $$RS$$ is a diameter of a circle, where $$R\!\left(\tfrac{4a}{5},-\tfrac{3b}{4}\right)$$ and $$S\!\left(\tfrac{2a}{5},\tfrac{5b}{4}\right).$$ Find the coordinates of the centre.
The line segment $$AB$$ is a diameter where $$A(3,-4),B(6,10).$$ (a) Find the centre of the circle. (b) Show that the circle lies on the line $$y=2x.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find midpoint for centre, substitute into line equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$C\!\left(\tfrac{9}{2},3\right).$$ (b) For $$y=2x\Rightarrow3=2(\tfrac{9}{2})\Rightarrow y=9,$$ true, so circle centre lies on the line.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line segment $$JK$$ is a diameter of a circle, with $$J(\tfrac{4}{3},\tfrac{4}{3})$$ and $$K(-\tfrac{1}{2},2).$$ The centre lies on line $$y=8x+b.$$ Find $$b.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find midpoint of $$JK$$, substitute into line to find $$b.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line segment $$AB$$ is a diameter of a circle, where $$A(0,-2),B(6,-5).$$ Show that the circle’s centre lies on the line $$x-2y-10=0.$$
The line segment $$FG$$ is a diameter of a circle centre $$C(6,1).$$ Given $$F(2,-3),$$ find $$G.$$
The line segment $$CD$$ is a diameter of a circle centre $$(-2a,5a).$$ Given $$D(3a,-7a),$$ find $$C.$$
Points $$M(3,p),N(4,q)$$ lie on a circle centre $$(5,6).$$ The diameter $$MN$$ has midpoint $$(5,6).$$ Find $$p,q.$$
The points $$V(-4,2a)$$ and $$W(3b,-4)$$ lie on the circle centre $$(b,2a).$$ The line segment $$VW$$ is a diameter of the circle. Find the values of $$a$$ and $$b.$$

A triangle has vertices $$A(3,5),\ B(7,11),\ C(p,q).$$ The midpoint of side $$BC$$ is $$M(8,5).$$ (a) Find $$p,q.$$ (b) Find the equation of the line joining the midpoint of $$AB$$ to $$M.$$ (c) Show that this line is parallel to $$AC.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use midpoint relation for (a); two-point form for (b); compare gradients for (c).
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$\tfrac{7+p}{2}=8,\ \tfrac{11+q}{2}=5\Rightarrow p=9,\ q=-1.$$ (b) Midpoint of $$AB=(5,8).$$ Gradient $$m=\tfrac{5-8}{8-5}=-1\Rightarrow y-8=-1(x-5)\Rightarrow x+y-13=0.$$ (c) Gradient of $$AC=\tfrac{-1-5}{9-3}=-1\Rightarrow\text{same gradient, so lines are parallel.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.hint: For each pair: midpoint $$M\!=\!\big(\tfrac{x_1+x_2}{2},\tfrac{y_1+y_2}{2}\big)$$ and slope $$m_{AB}=\tfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$$; bisector slope $$m_\perp=-\tfrac{1}{m_{AB}}$$ (if segment is vertical/horizontal handle separately); line through $$M$$ with slope $$m_\perp$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Examples shown: (a) $$M(1,5),\ m_{AB}=\tfrac{2-8}{7-(-5)}=-\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_\perp=2,\ y-5=2(x-1)\Rightarrow 2x-y+3=0.$$ (e) $$M(-\tfrac12,5),\ m_{ST}=\tfrac{-1-11}{-5-4}=\tfrac{12}{9}=\tfrac43\Rightarrow m_\perp=-\tfrac34,\ y-5=-\tfrac34\!\left(x+\tfrac12\right)\Rightarrow 3x+4y-17=0.$$ (f) horizontal segment: $$M(9,11),\ m_{XY}=0\Rightarrow \text{bisector }x=9.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line segment $$FG$$ is a diameter of a circle with centre $$C$$, where $$F(-2,5)$$ and $$G(2,9)$$. The line $$l$$ passes through $$C$$ and is perpendicular to $$FG$$. Find the equation of $$l$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find centre as midpoint of $$FG$$, slope of $$FG$$ then negative reciprocal.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line segment $$JK$$ is a diameter of a circle with centre $$P,$$ where $$J(0,-3)$$ and $$K(4,-5)$$. The line $$l$$ passes through $$P$$ and is perpendicular to $$JK$$. Find the equation of $$l$$ in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Midpoint for $$P$$; slope of $$JK,$$ take negative reciprocal and write line through $$P$$.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Points $$A(-4,-9),B(6,-3),C(11,5),D(-1,9).$$ (a) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of $$AB$$. (b) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of $$CD$$. (c) Find the coordinates of their point of intersection.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Midpoint+slope for each segment; bisector has slope negative reciprocal; solve two lines simultaneously.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$M_{AB}(1,-6),\ m_{AB}=\tfrac{-3-(-9)}{6-(-4)}=\tfrac35\Rightarrow m_\perp=-\tfrac53,\ y+6=-\tfrac53(x-1)\Rightarrow 5x+3y+13=0.$$ (b) $$M_{CD}(5,7),\ m_{CD}=\tfrac{9-5}{-1-11}=-\tfrac13\Rightarrow m_\perp=3,\ y-7=3(x-5)\Rightarrow 3x-y-8=0.$$ (c) Solve: $$\begin{cases}5x+3y+13=0\\3x-y-8=0\end{cases}\Rightarrow x=\tfrac{11}{14},\ y=-\tfrac{79}{14}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Point $$X(7,-2)$$ and point $$Y(4,q)$$. The perpendicular bisector of $$XY$$ has equation $$y=4x+b$$. Find the values of $$q$$ and $$b$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use slope condition $$m_\perp\cdot m_{XY}=-1$$ and midpoint lies on bisector.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Triangle $$PQR$$ has vertices $$P(6,9),Q(3,-3),R(-9,3).$$ (a) Find the perpendicular bisectors of each side of the triangle. (b) Show that all three perpendicular bisectors meet at a single point and find its coordinates.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Midpoints and perpendicular slopes for $$PQ,QR,PR$$; write their equations and solve any two to get the circumcenter.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Bisector of }PQ:\ 2x+8y-33=0;\quad \text{of }QR:\ 2x-y+6=0;\quad \text{of }PR:\ 10x+4y-9=0.$$ Solving (first two): $$x=-\tfrac{5}{6},\ y=\tfrac{13}{3}.$$ Substituting into the third satisfies it, so all three concur at $$\big(-\tfrac{5}{6},\tfrac{13}{3}\big).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The perpendicular bisectors of chords $$AB$$ and $$CD$$ of a circle intersect at $$O(4,-1).$$ Given $$A(2,3),B(6,1)$$ and $$C(1,-5),D(7,1),$$ verify that $$O$$ is equidistant from $$A,B,C,$$ and $$D.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use distance formula from $$O$$ to each point.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Points $$A(-2,4),B(6,0),C(4,8)$$ lie on a circle. Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find perpendicular bisectors of two sides.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Midpoint of $$AB=(2,2)$$ and slope $$m_{AB}=\tfrac{0-4}{6+2}=-\tfrac12$$ so bisector slope $$=2.$$ Equation $$y-2=2(x-2).$$ Midpoint of $$BC=(5,4)$$, slope $$=\tfrac{8-0}{4-6}=-4$$ so bisector slope $$=\tfrac14.$$ Solving gives centre $$O(2,2).$$ Radius $$r=\sqrt{(2+2)^2+(2-4)^2}=\sqrt{20}.$$ Equation $$ (x-2)^2+(y-2)^2=20.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Show that the perpendicular bisectors of $$AB,BC,$$ and $$CA$$ are concurrent for $$A(1,3),B(5,7),C(9,3).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find intersection of any two bisectors.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Midpoint of $$AB=(3,5),$$ slope $$=1$$ so bisector slope $$=-1.$$ Equation $$y-5=-1(x-3).$$ Midpoint of $$BC=(7,5),$$ slope $$=-1$$ so bisector slope $$=1.$$ Equation $$y-5=x-7.$$ Solving gives $$O(5,3).$$ Substituting into bisector of $$CA$$ satisfies equation, hence concurrent.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle is $$O(3,-2).$$ One chord has endpoints $$A(1,4)$$ and $$B(p,q).$$ If $$AB$$ is horizontal, find $$p,q.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Since $$AB$$ is horizontal, $$q=4.$$ Midpoint of $$AB=\left(\tfrac{1+p}{2},4\right).$$ The perpendicular from centre meets midpoint vertically, so $$\tfrac{1+p}{2}=3\Rightarrow p=5.$$ Hence $$B(5,4).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: One end of a diameter is $$A(-1,6)$$ and the centre is $$O(4,-2).$$ Find the other end $$B.$$
Find the equation of the locus of points equidistant from $$A(2,-1)$$ and $$B(8,5).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Midpoint $$M(5,2).$$ Slope $$m_{AB}=1$$ so bisector slope $$=-1.$$ Equation $$y-2=-1(x-5)\Rightarrow x+y-7=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The endpoints of a chord are $$A(-4,1),B(8,1).$$ The centre lies on $$x=2.$$ Find the radius.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Midpoint $$M(2,1).$$ Distance $$OM=0.$$ Length of chord $$=12,$$ so radius $$=\tfrac{12}{2}=6.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle lies on $$y=2x-1$$ and is equidistant from $$A(1,3)$$ and $$B(5,1).$$ Find the centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Intersect perpendicular bisector with given line.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Midpoint $$M(3,2).$$ Slope $$m_{AB}=-\tfrac12,$$ bisector slope $$=2.$$ Equation $$y-2=2(x-3)\Rightarrow y=2x-4.$$ Solving with $$y=2x-1$$ gives $$O(2,3).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Show that the triangle with vertices $$A(2,1),B(6,5),C(10,1)$$ is right-angled at $$B.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$m_{AB}=\tfrac{5-1}{6-2}=1,\ m_{BC}=\tfrac{1-5}{10-6}=-1.$$ Since gradients are negative reciprocals, $$AB\perp BC,$$ hence right-angled at $$B.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the equation of a circle whose centre lies on $$y=x+1$$ and passes through $$A(1,2)$$ and $$B(5,6).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use perpendicular bisector and given line.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Midpoint $$M(3,4).$$ Slope $$m_{AB}=1,$$ bisector slope $$=-1.$$ Equation $$y-4=-1(x-3)\Rightarrow y=-x+7.$$ Solving with $$y=x+1$$ gives centre $$O(3,4).$$ Radius $$=\sqrt{8}.$$ Equation $$ (x-3)^2+(y-4)^2=8.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The point $$B$$ is the reflection of $$A(2,-3)$$ across the line $$x+y=1.$$ Find $$B.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find foot of perpendicular then reflect.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The diameter of a circle has slope $$2$$ and midpoint $$M(3,-1).$$ Find the equation of the diameter perpendicular to it.
The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of an isosceles triangle are concurrent. Prove this.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Since two sides are equal, their perpendicular bisectors intersect on the axis of symmetry, which also bisects the third side, hence all meet at one point.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of the circumcircle of triangle $$ABC$$ is $$O(0,0).$$ If $$A(4,0),B(0,4),$$ find $$C.$$
Points $$A(-2,1),B(4,3),C(2,-3)$$ lie on a circle. Verify.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Bisectors intersect at $$O(1,0).$$ Distances $$OA=OB=OC,$$ hence points are concyclic.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A vertical chord has endpoints $$A(3,2),B(3,10).$$ The centre lies on $$y=4x-1.$$ Find the centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Midpoint $$M(3,6).$$ Bisector $$y=6.$$ Solve with $$y=4x-1$$ gives $$x=\tfrac74.$$ Hence centre $$\left(\tfrac74,6\right).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Show that the line joining midpoints of two chords is parallel to the line joining their endpoints.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Both gradients are equal by midpoint theorem, hence lines are parallel.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the radical axis of the circles $$x^2+y^2=25$$ and $$(x-4)^2+y^2=9.$$
Points $$A(1,2),B(5,6),C(k,4)$$ lie on a circle whose centre lies on $$y=x.$$ Find $$k.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Using perpendicular bisector and $$y=x$$ gives centre $$O(3,3).$$ Distance equality gives $$k=3.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Centre from bisector and line constraint
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre $$O(h,k)$$ of a circle lies on $$2x-y+3=0$$ and is equidistant from $$A(1,2)$$ and $$B(7,4).$$ Find $$O.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find the perpendicular bisector of }AB\text{ and intersect it with }2x-y+3=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Show that $$A(0,2),B(4,6),C(8,10)$$ do not determine a unique circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Check if the points are collinear; then perpendicular bisectors won’t meet uniquely.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$m_{AB}=\tfrac{6-2}{4-0}=1,\quad m_{BC}=\tfrac{10-6}{8-4}=1\Rightarrow A,B,C\text{ are collinear.}$$ $$\text{A circle through three collinear points is impossible (no unique centre), so no unique circumcircle exists.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the equation of the circle through $$A(-3,1),B(5,7),C(1,-1).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find perpendicular bisectors of }AB\text{ and }AC,\text{ intersect to get the centre.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$M_{AB}\left(\tfrac{-3+5}{2},\tfrac{1+7}{2}\right)=(1,4),\ m_{AB}=\tfrac{7-1}{5-(-3)}=\tfrac{6}{8}=\tfrac34\Rightarrow m_\perp=-\tfrac43.$$ $$\Rightarrow \text{Bisector of }AB:\ y-4=-\tfrac43(x-1).$$ $$M_{AC}\left(\tfrac{-3+1}{2},\tfrac{1+(-1)}{2}\right)=(-1,0),\ m_{AC}=\tfrac{-1-1}{1-(-3)}=-\tfrac{2}{4}=-\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_\perp=2.$$ $$\Rightarrow \text{Bisector of }AC:\ y-0=2(x+1)\Rightarrow y=2x+2.$$ $$\text{Substitute into first: }2x+2-4=-\tfrac43(x-1)\Rightarrow 2x-2=-\tfrac43x+\tfrac43.$$ $$\Rightarrow \tfrac{10}{3}x=\tfrac{10}{3}\Rightarrow x=1,\ y=4.$$ $$O(1,4),\ r^2=OA^2=(1+3)^2+(4-1)^2=16+9=25.$$ $$\therefore (x-1)^2+(y-4)^2=25.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Centre lies on axis; find radius
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through $$A(-2,5)$$ and $$B(6,1).$$ Its centre lies on the line $$x=2.$$ Find the centre and the circle equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre is intersection of }x=2\text{ with the perpendicular bisector of }AB.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has centre $$O(4,-3).$$ The chord $$AB$$ lies on the line $$3x+4y-10=0$$ and is cut at right angles by the line from $$O$$. Find the midpoint of chord $$AB.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{The midpoint is the foot of perpendicular from }O\text{ to the chord line.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Chord line: }3x+4y-10=0\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac34x+\tfrac52,\ m=-\tfrac34.$$ $$\Rightarrow \text{Perpendicular slope }m_\perp=\tfrac43.$$ $$\text{Line through }O: y+3=\tfrac43(x-4).$$ $$\text{Intersect with }3x+4y-10=0: \ y=\tfrac43(x-4)-3=\tfrac43x-\tfrac{25}{3}.$$ $$3x+4\left(\tfrac43x-\tfrac{25}{3}\right)-10=0\Rightarrow 3x+\tfrac{16}{3}x-\tfrac{100}{3}-10=0.$$ $$\Rightarrow \tfrac{25}{3}x-\tfrac{130}{3}=0\Rightarrow x=\tfrac{26}{5}.$$ $$y=\tfrac43\cdot\tfrac{26}{5}-\tfrac{25}{3}=\tfrac{104}{15}-\tfrac{125}{15}=-\tfrac{21}{15}=-\tfrac75.$$ $$\therefore \text{Midpoint }M\left(\tfrac{26}{5},-\tfrac75\right).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find chord length from radius and distance
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The radius of a circle is $$13$$. A chord is at perpendicular distance $$5$$ from the centre. Find the chord length.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Parameter for centre on a line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle passes through $$A(0,0)$$ and $$B(8,0).$$ Its centre lies on $$y=x-2.$$ Find the centre(s) and equation(s) of the circle(s).
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre lies on perpendicular bisector of }AB\text{ and on }y=x-2.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$AB\text{ is horizontal, midpoint }M(4,0),\ \text{bisector is }x=4.$$ $$\text{Intersect with }y=x-2:\ x=4\Rightarrow y=2.$$ $$O(4,2).$$ $$r^2=OA^2=4^2+2^2=20.$$ $$\therefore x^2+y^2-8x-4y=0\ \text{or}\ (x-4)^2+(y-2)^2=20.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Given $$A(1,1),B(7,1),C(1,9),$$ (a) show $$\angle A$$ is a right angle, (b) find the circumcentre, (c) find the circumcircle equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Use slopes for (a), then midpoint of hypotenuse for (b).}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$(a)\ m_{AB}=0,\ m_{AC}=\infty\Rightarrow AB\perp AC\Rightarrow \angle A=90^\circ.$$ $$(b)\ \text{Hypotenuse is }BC,\ M_{BC}\left(\tfrac{7+1}{2},\tfrac{1+9}{2}\right)=(4,5)\Rightarrow O(4,5).$$ $$(c)\ r^2=OB^2=(4-7)^2+(5-1)^2=9+16=25.$$ $$\therefore (x-4)^2+(y-5)^2=25.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The reflection of $$A(6,-2)$$ in the line $$x-2y+4=0$$ is $$A'$$. Find $$A'.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find foot of perpendicular from }A\text{ to the line, then reflect.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Line: }x-2y+4=0\Rightarrow y=\tfrac12x+2,\ m=\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_\perp=-2.$$ $$\text{Perpendicular through }A:\ y+2=-2(x-6)\Rightarrow y=-2x+10.$$ $$\text{Intersect with }y=\tfrac12x+2:\ -2x+10=\tfrac12x+2\Rightarrow -\tfrac52x=-8\Rightarrow x=\tfrac{16}{5}.$$ $$y=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{16}{5}+2=\tfrac{8}{5}+\tfrac{10}{5}=\tfrac{18}{5}.$$ $$\text{Foot }M\left(\tfrac{16}{5},\tfrac{18}{5}\right).$$ $$\text{Reflection: }A'=2M-A=\left(\tfrac{32}{5}-6,\tfrac{36}{5}-(-2)\right)=\left(\tfrac{2}{5},\tfrac{46}{5}\right).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Radical axis from two circle equations
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the radical axis of $$x^2+y^2-6x+2y-7=0$$ and $$x^2+y^2+2x-4y-5=0.$$
In a circle, chords $$AB$$ and $$CD$$ have midpoints $$M(2,1)$$ and $$N(6,5)$$ respectively. Chord $$AB$$ has slope $$1$$ and chord $$CD$$ has slope $$-2.$$ Find the centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre lies on lines through midpoints perpendicular to each chord.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Chord }AB\ m=1\Rightarrow \text{radius line through }M\text{ has }m_\perp=-1:\ y-1=-1(x-2)\Rightarrow x+y-3=0.$$ $$\text{Chord }CD\ m=-2\Rightarrow \text{radius line through }N\text{ has }m_\perp=\tfrac12:\ y-5=\tfrac12(x-6)\Rightarrow x-2y+4=0.$$ $$\text{Solve } \begin{cases}x+y-3=0\\x-2y+4=0\end{cases}\Rightarrow y=\tfrac{7}{3},\ x=\tfrac{2}{3}.$$ $$\therefore O\left(\tfrac23,\tfrac73\right).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle has equation $$x^2+y^2+Dx+Ey+F=0$$ and passes through $$A(0,0),B(6,0),C(0,8).$$ Find $$D,E,F$$ and the centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Substitute the three points to form three equations in }D,E,F.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find chord equation from its midpoint and circle centre
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle has centre $$O(1,-2).$$ A chord has midpoint $$M(5,4).$$ Find the equation of the chord.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Chord is perpendicular to }OM\text{ and passes through }M.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Distance from centre to chord line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has centre $$O(-2,3)$$ and radius $$10.$$ The chord lies on $$3x-4y+12=0.$$ Find the chord length.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find distance }d\text{ from centre to line; then }L=2\sqrt{r^2-d^2}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find parameter so centre lies on y-axis
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle through $$A(2,1),B(6,5),C(k,3)$$ has its centre on the $$y$$-axis. Find $$k.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Compute circumcentre in terms of }k\text{ and set }x_O=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Two possible centres from line constraint
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through $$A(1,4)$$ and $$B(9,4).$$ Its centre lies on $$x+y=10.$$ Find the centre(s).
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre is on perpendicular bisector }x=5\text{ and on }x+y=10.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle through two points with fixed radius
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle of radius $$5$$ passes through $$A(0,0)$$ and $$B(6,0).$$ Find the possible centres.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centres lie on perpendicular bisector of }AB\text{ and satisfy distance }5\text{ from }A.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find equation of circle from diameter endpoints
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The endpoints of a diameter are $$A(-4,2)$$ and $$B(8,-6).$$ Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre is midpoint; radius is distance to an endpoint.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the point $$P(x,y)$$ that is equidistant from $$A(1,1),B(5,3),C(3,7).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle equation from centre and tangent line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Circle centre is $$O(3,1).$$ The line $$x-2y+5=0$$ is tangent to the circle. Find the circle equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Radius = distance from centre to tangent line.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find chord endpoints from midpoint and slope
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A chord has midpoint $$M(2,-1)$$ and slope $$\tfrac{3}{4}.$$ Its length is $$10.$$ Find its endpoints.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{A direction vector for slope }\tfrac34\text{ is }(4,3),\ \|(4,3)\|=5.$$ $$\text{Half-chord vector }=5\cdot\frac{(4,3)}{5}=(4,3).$$ $$\Rightarrow A=M-(4,3)=(-2,-4),\ B=M+(4,3)=(6,2).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Centre lies on a given segment bisector
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre is equidistant from $$A(-1,2)$$ and $$B(7,6)$$ and also lies on $$y=1.$$ Find the centre.
The circle is $$x^2+y^2=100.$$ The chord is cut by the line $$y=6.$$ Find the chord length.
Prove: In the same circle, equal chords are equidistant from the centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Use perpendicular from centre to each chord and congruent right triangles.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Let equal chords }AB\text{ and }CD\text{ have midpoints }M,N\text{ with }OM\perp AB,\ ON\perp CD.$$ $$AM=CM=\tfrac12AB=\tfrac12CD=CN.$$ $$OA=OC\text{ (radii).}$$ $$\triangle OMA\cong \triangle ONC\text{ (RHS), hence }OM=ON.$$ $$\therefore \text{equal chords are equidistant from the centre.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle with centre $$O(2,3)$$ passes through $$A(6,3).$$ Find $$k$$ such that the line $$y=kx+1$$ is tangent to the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Radius from }O\text{ to }A,\ \text{then set distance from }O\text{ to line equal to radius.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$r=OA=\sqrt{(6-2)^2+(3-3)^2}=4.$$ $$\text{Line }y=kx+1\Rightarrow kx-y+1=0.$$ $$\text{Distance }d=\frac{|2k-3+1|}{\sqrt{k^2+1}}=\frac{|2k-2|}{\sqrt{k^2+1}}.$$ $$\text{Tangency: }d=4\Rightarrow \frac{|2(k-1)|}{\sqrt{k^2+1}}=4\Rightarrow |k-1|=2\sqrt{k^2+1}.$$ $$\text{Square: }(k-1)^2=4(k^2+1)\Rightarrow k^2-2k+1=4k^2+4\Rightarrow 3k^2+2k+3=0.$$ $$\Delta=4-36=-32<0\Rightarrow \text{no real }k\text{ (no tangent of that form).}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the circumcircle of $$A(0,0),B(4,2),C(2,6).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$M_{AB}(2,1),\ m_{AB}=\tfrac{2}{4}=\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_\perp=-2.$$ $$\Rightarrow y-1=-2(x-2)\Rightarrow y=-2x+5.$$ $$M_{AC}(1,3),\ m_{AC}=\tfrac{6}{2}=3\Rightarrow m_\perp=-\tfrac13.$$ $$\Rightarrow y-3=-\tfrac13(x-1)\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac13x+\tfrac{10}{3}.$$ $$\text{Intersect: }-2x+5=-\tfrac13x+\tfrac{10}{3}\Rightarrow -\tfrac{5}{3}x=-\tfrac{5}{3}\Rightarrow x=1,\ y=3.$$ $$O(1,3),\ r^2=1^2+3^2=10.$$ $$\therefore (x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=10.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Locus of points with fixed midpoint
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The midpoint of segment joining $$P(x,y)$$ to $$Q(6,-2)$$ is always on the line $$x+y=5.$$ Find the locus of $$P.$$
The centre of a circle is equidistant from $$A(2,0)$$ and $$B(0,2)$$ and lies on $$y=x.$$ Find the centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$M(1,1),\ m_{AB}=\tfrac{2-0}{0-2}=-1\Rightarrow m_\perp=1.$$ $$\text{Bisector: }y-1=1(x-1)\Rightarrow y=x.$$ $$\text{So the bisector is the same as }y=x\Rightarrow \text{infinitely many centres on }y=x.$$ $$\text{Any }O(t,t)\text{ satisfies }OA=OB\ (\text{symmetry}).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the perpendicular bisector of $$A\left(\tfrac12,-3\right)$$ and $$B\left(\tfrac{9}{2},5\right)$$ in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$ with integers.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find midpoint and slope, then write line and clear fractions.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Hard composite: centre, chord, and parallelism
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle has diameter endpoints $$A(1,5)$$ and $$B(9,1).$$ (a) Find the circle equation. (b) Find the equation of the tangent at point $$A.$$ (c) Show this tangent is parallel to the perpendicular bisector of $$AB.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{(a) midpoint and radius; (b) radius }OA\perp \text{tangent; (c) compare gradients.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$(a)\ O\left(\tfrac{1+9}{2},\tfrac{5+1}{2}\right)=(5,3).$$ $$r^2=OA^2=(5-1)^2+(3-5)^2=16+4=20\Rightarrow (x-5)^2+(y-3)^2=20.$$ $$(b)\ m_{OA}=\tfrac{5-3}{1-5}=\tfrac{2}{-4}=-\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_{\text{tangent}}=2.$$ $$\text{Tangent at }A:\ y-5=2(x-1)\Rightarrow 2x-y+3=0.$$ $$(c)\ m_{AB}=\tfrac{1-5}{9-1}=-\tfrac{4}{8}=-\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_{\perp\ \text{bisector}}=2.$$ $$\text{Tangent gradient }=2=\text{bisector gradient}\Rightarrow \text{parallel.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Given the circle $$x^2+y^2+2ax-8y+3a=0$$ where $$a$$ is a constant. (a) Write it in the form $$(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2.$$ (b) Find the centre and radius in terms of $$a.$$ (c) Find the range of $$a$$ for which the circle is real.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Group }x\text{ terms and }y\text{ terms, complete squares; require }r^2>0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line segment joining $$A(-5,3)$$ and $$B(7,-1)$$ is a diameter of a circle. Find the equation of the circle.
Find the equation of the circle passing through $$A(1,2),\ B(5,-2),\ C(7,4).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Let }x^2+y^2+Dx+Ey+F=0.$$ $$A:\ 1+4+D+2E+F=0\Rightarrow D+2E+F=-5.$$ $$B:\ 25+4+5D-2E+F=0\Rightarrow5D-2E+F=-29.$$ $$C:\ 49+16+7D+4E+F=0\Rightarrow7D+4E+F=-65.$$ $$\text{Subtract (B)-(A): }4D-4E=-24\Rightarrow D-E=-6.$$ $$\text{Subtract (C)-(A): }6D+2E=-60\Rightarrow3D+E=-30.$$ $$D=E-6\Rightarrow3(E-6)+E=-30\Rightarrow4E=-12\Rightarrow E=-3,\ D=-9.$$ $$D+2E+F=-5\Rightarrow -9-6+F=-5\Rightarrow F=10.$$ $$\therefore x^2+y^2-9x-3y+10=0.$$ $$\text{Complete squares: }(x-\tfrac92)^2+(y-\tfrac32)^2=\tfrac{41}{2}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Centre and radius from general form
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Given $$x^2+y^2-12x+6y+11=0,$$ find the centre and radius.
The circle $$x^2+y^2-6x+2y+k=0$$ is tangent to the $$x$$-axis. Find $$k.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Tangency to }x\text{-axis means distance from centre to }y=0\text{ equals }r.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x^2-6x+y^2+2y+k=0\Rightarrow(x-3)^2+(y+1)^2=10-k.$$ $$\text{Centre }(3,-1),\ r^2=10-k.$$ $$\text{Distance to }y=0\text{ is }1,$$ so $$r=1\Rightarrow r^2=1.$$ $$10-k=1\Rightarrow k=9.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle is tangent to both coordinate axes and passes through the point $$P(6,8).$$ Find its equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{If tangent to both axes in first quadrant, centre }(r,r). Use P\text{ to solve.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Equation from centre and chord midpoint
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle has centre $$C(2,-3).$$ A chord has midpoint $$M(6,1)$$ and length $$8.$$ Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Distance }CM\text{ gives distance from centre to chord; use }(\tfrac{L}{2})^2=r^2-d^2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The diameter of a circle lies on the line $$3x-4y+10=0$$ and its endpoints are the points where this line meets the circle $$x^2+y^2=25.$$ Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find endpoints by solving with }3x-4y+10=0;\ \text{centre is midpoint; radius is half the distance.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$3x-4y+10=0\Rightarrow y=\tfrac34x+\tfrac52.$$ $$x^2+\left(\tfrac34x+\tfrac52\right)^2=25\Rightarrow x^2+\tfrac{9}{16}x^2+\tfrac{15}{4}x+\tfrac{25}{4}=25.$$ $$\tfrac{25}{16}x^2+\tfrac{15}{4}x-\tfrac{75}{4}=0\Rightarrow25x^2+60x-300=0\Rightarrow5x^2+12x-60=0.$$ $$x=\frac{-12\pm\sqrt{144+1200}}{10}=\frac{-12\pm4\sqrt{84}}{10}=\frac{-6\pm4\sqrt{21}}{5}.$$ $$y=\tfrac34x+\tfrac52=\frac{16\pm3\sqrt{21}}{5}.$$ $$\text{Midpoint }C=\left(\tfrac{-6/5}{},\tfrac{16/5}{}\right)=\left(-\tfrac65,\tfrac{16}{5}\right).$$ $$r^2=25-\left(\text{distance from origin to }C\right)^2\text{ not needed; use }r^2=CA^2=\frac{(4\sqrt{21})^2+(6\sqrt{21})^2}{(5)^2\cdot4}=\frac{21\cdot52}{25}=\frac{1092}{25}.$$ $$\therefore \left(x+\tfrac65\right)^2+\left(y-\tfrac{16}{5}\right)^2=\tfrac{1092}{25}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find circle from two opposite points
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Two points $$A(1,7)$$ and $$B(9,-1)$$ are opposite ends of a diameter. A point $$P(x,y)$$ lies on the circle. Show that $$x^2+y^2-10x-6y+9=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Determine r from point on circle
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The point $$(-3,11)$$ lies on the circle $$(x-3)^2+(y+4)^2=r^2.$$ Find $$r.$$
The circle has equation $$(x-a)^2+(y+2)^2=29$$ and passes through $$P(5,1).$$ Find $$a.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find k so circle passes through two points
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2+4x-6y+k=0$$ passes through $$A(0,0)$$ and $$B(2,4).$$ Find $$k.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Substitute each point; solve for }k\text{ and check consistency.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$A(0,0):\ k=0.$$ $$B(2,4):\ 4+16+8-24+k=0\Rightarrow4+k=0\Rightarrow k=-4.$$ $$\text{Contradiction, so no such }k\text{ exists.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Equation of circle through intersection of lines
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle is the intersection of the lines $$2x-y=1$$ and $$x+3y=11.$$ The circle passes through $$P(5,4).$$ Find the equation of the circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with centre on a line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle lies on $$x-2y+1=0$$ and the circle passes through $$A(1,2)$$ and $$B(7,4).$$ Find the equation(s) of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre lies on perpendicular bisector of }AB\text{ and on given line.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle orthogonal to x-axis and y-axis
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through the origin and has its centre on the line $$y=x+2.$$ Also, it passes through $$P(4,2).$$ Find the equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Let centre }(h,k)\text{ with }k=h+2.\ Use O\text{ and }P\text{ constraints.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Since }(0,0)\text{ on circle: }h^2+k^2=r^2.$$ $$\text{Since }(4,2)\text{ on circle: }(4-h)^2+(2-k)^2=r^2.$$ $$\Rightarrow (4-h)^2+(2-k)^2=h^2+k^2.$$ $$16-8h+h^2+4-4k+k^2=h^2+k^2\Rightarrow20-8h-4k=0\Rightarrow2h+k=5.$$ $$k=h+2\Rightarrow2h+h+2=5\Rightarrow h=1,\ k=3.$$ $$r^2=h^2+k^2=10.$$ $$\therefore (x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=10.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Given $$x^2+y^2-4x+2y-4=0,$$ find where the circle cuts the axes.
The circle has centre $$C(2,-1)$$ and is tangent to the line $$3x+4y-20=0.$$ Find its equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Radius = distance from centre to tangent line.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle through a point and tangent to axis
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through $$P(6,0)$$ and is tangent to the $$y$$-axis. Its centre lies on the line $$y=2.$$ Find the equation(s) of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Tangency to }y\text{-axis means centre }(r,2)\text{ or }(-r,2)\text{ with }r>0. Use point.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through $$A(2,1)$$ and $$B(8,5).$$ Find the locus of its centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre must lie on perpendicular bisector of }AB.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with diameter on coordinate axes
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle has diameter endpoints on the axes at $$A(a,0)$$ and $$B(0,b)$$ and passes through $$P(2,3).$$ Given $$a=8,$$ find $$b$$ and the circle equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Use diameter endpoints to get centre and radius; substitute }P\text{ to solve }b.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Equation from centre on perpendicular bisector
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through $$A(0,6)$$ and $$B(8,0).$$ Its centre lies on the line $$x=2.$$ Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre is intersection of }x=2\text{ with perpendicular bisector of }AB.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find circle given tangent at a point
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through $$A(3,4)$$ and has centre on the line $$y=4$$. The tangent at $$A$$ is perpendicular to the line $$x+2y-11=0.$$ Find the circle equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Tangent }\perp\text{ radius at }A.\ \text{Use slopes to get radius line; intersect with }y=4.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x+2y-11=0\Rightarrow y=-\tfrac12x+\tfrac{11}{2}\Rightarrow m=-\tfrac12.$$ $$\text{Tangent }\perp \text{ this }\Rightarrow m_{\text{tan}}=2.$$ $$\text{Radius at }A\perp\text{ tangent }\Rightarrow m_{CA}=-\tfrac12.$$ $$\text{Line }CA:\ y-4=-\tfrac12(x-3).$$ $$\text{Centre lies on }y=4:\ 0=-\tfrac12(x-3)\Rightarrow x=3.$$ $$\Rightarrow C(3,4)\Rightarrow r=0\ (\text{degenerate}).$$ $$\text{So no non-degenerate circle satisfies the conditions.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find k so circle touches line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2-4x+6y+k=0$$ touches the line $$x-2y+7=0.$$ Find $$k.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Determine equation from two tangency conditions
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle is tangent to both lines $$x=1$$ and $$y=-2$$ and passes through $$P(5,4).$$ Find the equation(s).
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Tangency gives centre }(1\pm r,-2\pm r).\ Use point to solve.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Let centre }(h,k),\ r>0.$$ $$\text{Tangency to }x=1\Rightarrow |h-1|=r,\ \text{to }y=-2\Rightarrow |k+2|=r.$$ $$\Rightarrow h=1\pm r,\ k=-2\pm r\ (\text{independent signs}).$$ $$\text{Use }(5,4):\ (5-h)^2+(4-k)^2=r^2.$$ $$\text{Case }h=1+r,\ k=-2+r:\ (4-r)^2+(6-r)^2=r^2\Rightarrow(16-8r+r^2)+(36-12r+r^2)=r^2.$$ $$52-20r+r^2=0\Rightarrow r=10\pm4\sqrt3.$$ $$\text{Valid }r>0\Rightarrow r=10+4\sqrt3\ \text{or}\ 10-4\sqrt3.$$ $$\Rightarrow (x-(1+r))^2+(y-(-2+r))^2=r^2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Line of centres for a family
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Circles in the family $$x^2+y^2-2tx+6y+9=0$$ depend on real parameter $$t.$$ Find the locus of their centres.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find equation given two intersection points with axes
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle cuts the axes at $$A(4,0),\ B(-2,0),\ C(0,3),\ D(0,-5).$$ Find its equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$A(4,0):\ 16+4D+F=0.$$ $$B(-2,0):\ 4-2D+F=0.$$ $$C(0,3):\ 9+3E+F=0.$$ $$D(0,-5):\ 25-5E+F=0.$$ $$\text{From A and B: }(16+4D+F)-(4-2D+F)=0\Rightarrow12+6D=0\Rightarrow D=-2.$$ $$4-2(-2)+F=0\Rightarrow8+F=0\Rightarrow F=-8.$$ $$\text{From C: }9+3E-8=0\Rightarrow3E+1=0\Rightarrow E=-\tfrac13.$$ $$\text{Check D: }25-5(-\tfrac13)-8=17+\tfrac53\neq0\Rightarrow \text{inconsistent data, no such circle.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with given centre and passing through line intersection
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle is the intersection of $$x+2y=7$$ and $$3x-y=5.$$ The circle also passes through the intersection of $$x=1$$ and $$y=-4.$$ Find the circle equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find centre by solving; radius from centre to }(1,-4).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find parameter so circle is tangent to y-axis
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2-8x+2y+p=0$$ is tangent to the $$y$$-axis. Find $$p.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Complete squares, then impose distance centre to }x=0\text{ equals }r.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x^2-8x+y^2+2y+p=0\Rightarrow(x-4)^2+(y+1)^2=17-p.$$ $$C(4,-1),\ r^2=17-p.$$ $$\text{Distance to }y\text{-axis }x=0\text{ is }4,$$ so $$r=4\Rightarrow r^2=16.$$ $$17-p=16\Rightarrow p=1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Two possible circles from a chord and radius
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle has radius $$5$$ and passes through $$A(0,0)$$ and $$B(6,0).$$ Find the possible equations of the circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find circle from chord endpoints and centre condition
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through $$A(2,5)$$ and $$B(10,1).$$ Its centre lies on the line $$y=-x+9.$$ Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre is intersection of perpendicular bisector of }AB\text{ with }y=-x+9.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Radius from tangency to a line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has centre $$C(4,-1)$$ and is tangent to the line $$3x+4y-20=0.$$ Find the equation of the circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle passes through $$A(1,4)$$ and $$B(7,-2)$$ and its centre lies on the $$x$$-axis. Find the equation(s) of the circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle through two points with centre on a given line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle passes through $$A(2,1)$$ and $$B(8,5).$$ Its centre lies on the line $$x-y=1.$$ Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre is intersection of perpendicular bisector of }AB\text{ with }x-y=1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Given $$x^2+y^2+6x-4y+k=0,$$ find the range of $$k$$ for which the equation represents a real circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle tangent to x-axis and y-axis
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle is tangent to both axes and has centre in the second quadrant. Its radius is $$r$$ and it passes through $$P(-6,5).$$ Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Second quadrant tangency gives centre }(-r,r). Substitute point.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Equation from chord and centre distance
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle has radius $$13$$. A chord of the circle has length $$10$$ and its midpoint is $$M(4,-3).$$ The centre lies on the line $$x+2y=1.$$ Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Distance centre to chord is }d=\sqrt{r^2-(L/2)^2}. Centre lies on perpendicular through M\text{ and on given line.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$r=13,\ \tfrac{L}{2}=5\Rightarrow d=\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=\sqrt{169-25}=12.$$ $$\text{The centre }C\text{ is 12 units from }M\text{ along a perpendicular to chord, but chord direction is unknown.}$$ $$\text{So there are infinitely many circles unless chord direction is specified. Therefore not uniquely determined.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle passing through origin and tangent to x-axis at origin
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through the origin and is tangent to the $$x$$-axis at the origin. It also passes through $$P(4,6).$$ Find the equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Tangency at origin implies centre lies on }y\text{-axis, say }(0,a),\ r=|a|.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with diameter endpoints involving parameter
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$A(t,2)$$ and $$B(6,-4)$$ are endpoints of a diameter of a circle. The circle passes through the origin. Find possible values of $$t$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Use angle in a semicircle: }OA\cdot OB? \text{Or compute equation via centre and impose }(0,0)\text{ on circle.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle through three points with one on axis
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the equation of the circle passing through $$A(0,4),\ B(6,0),\ C(4,6).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$A:\ 16+4E+F=0\Rightarrow4E+F=-16.$$ $$B:\ 36+6D+F=0\Rightarrow6D+F=-36.$$ $$C:\ 16+36+4D+6E+F=0\Rightarrow4D+6E+F=-52.$$ $$F=-16-4E,\ F=-36-6D\Rightarrow -16-4E=-36-6D\Rightarrow6D-4E=-20\Rightarrow3D-2E=-10.$$ $$Use in third: 4D+6E-16-4E=-52\Rightarrow4D+2E=-36\Rightarrow2D+E=-18.$$ $$Solve: E=-18-2D. Substitute into 3D-2E=-10: 3D-2(-18-2D)=-10\Rightarrow3D+36+4D=-10\Rightarrow7D=-46\Rightarrow D=-\tfrac{46}{7}.$$ $$E=-18-2(-\tfrac{46}{7})=-\tfrac{34}{7}.$$ $$F=-36-6D=-36+ \tfrac{276}{7}=\tfrac{24}{7}.$$ $$\therefore x^2+y^2-\tfrac{46}{7}x-\tfrac{34}{7}y+\tfrac{24}{7}=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with centre on perpendicular bisector and fixed radius
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has radius $$10$$ and passes through $$A(2,3)$$ and $$B(14,3).$$ Find its equation(s).
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centres lie on perpendicular bisector of }AB\text{ at }x=8,\ \text{and distance to }A\text{ is }10.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle touching x-axis with fixed centre x-coordinate
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle has $$x$$-coordinate $$4$$ and the circle touches the $$x$$-axis. It passes through $$P(10,5).$$ Find the equation(s) of the circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find k so circle passes through intersection of two lines
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2-6x+2y+k=0$$ passes through the intersection point of $$x+y=1$$ and $$2x-y=5.$$ Find $$k.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find intersection point then substitute into circle.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Parameter for circle with given centre distance to origin
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2+2ax-4y+1=0$$ has its centre at distance $$5$$ from the origin. Find $$a$$.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with centre on y-axis and passing through two points
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has its centre on the $$y$$-axis and passes through $$A(2,1)$$ and $$B(-4,5).$$ Find its equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Let centre }(0,k). Equate distances to A and B to solve for k.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Equation from tangent at a given point (general form)
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle passes through $$P(3,4)$$ and has equation $$x^2+y^2+Dx+Ey+F=0.$$ The tangent at $$P$$ is $$3x-4y+7=0.$$ Find $$D,E,F$$ and the circle equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Centre }(-\tfrac{D}{2},-\tfrac{E}{2}),\ \nabla: 2x+D,\ 2y+E.$$ $$\text{Normal to tangent }3x-4y+7=0\text{ is }(3,-4),\ \text{so radius at }P\text{ has direction }(3,-4).$$ $$\text{Thus }(2x+D,2y+E)\big|_{(3,4)}=(6+D,8+E)\parallel(3,-4).$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{6+D}{3}=\frac{8+E}{-4}=\lambda.$$ $$6+D=3\lambda,\ 8+E=-4\lambda.$$ $$Also P\text{ on circle: }9+16+3D+4E+F=0\Rightarrow3D+4E+F=-25.$$ $$But we need one more condition: tangent line must match exactly, not just direction. Use tangent formula: at (3,4),\ 3x+4y+\frac{D}{2}(x+3)+\frac{E}{2}(y+4)+F=0.$$ $$This must be proportional to 3x-4y+7=0\text{ which is impossible because }(3,4)\not\parallel(3,-4).$$ $$\therefore \text{no such circle exists with that tangent at }P.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with given diameter and tangency
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The diameter endpoints of a circle are $$A(0,2)$$ and $$B(8,6).$$ Show the circle is tangent to the line $$x-2y+4=0$$ or explain why not.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find centre and radius; compute distance from centre to line and compare to }r.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$C(4,4),\ r^2=CA^2=(4-0)^2+(4-2)^2=16+4=20,\ r=\sqrt{20}.$$ $$d=\frac{|4-2(4)+4|}{\sqrt{1^2+(-2)^2}}=\frac{|4-8+4|}{\sqrt5}=0.$$ $$d\neq r\Rightarrow \text{not tangent (line passes through centre).}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find radius given general equation constraint
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2-2px+6y+9=0$$ has radius $$5.$$ Find $$p.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with centre on x-axis and tangent to a line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle has centre on the $$x$$-axis and is tangent to the line $$y=x-4.$$ It passes through $$P(2,0).$$ Find the equation(s) of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Let centre }(h,0),\ r=|h-2|. Tangency gives distance centre-line = r.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find equation from intercept form condition
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has centre $$C(h,k)$$ and passes through the origin. It cuts the positive axes at $$A(a,0)$$ and $$B(0,b)$$ with $$a=b.$$ Find the circle equation in terms of $$a.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Use points }(0,0),(a,0),(0,a)\text{ on circle; solve for centre.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{By symmetry, centre lies on }y=x\Rightarrow k=h.$$ $$\text{Circle through }(0,0):\ h^2+k^2=r^2=2h^2.$$ $$\text{Through }(a,0):\ (a-h)^2+h^2=2h^2\Rightarrow(a-h)^2=h^2\Rightarrow a-h=\pm h.$$ $$a=0\text{ or }a=2h\Rightarrow h=\tfrac{a}{2},\ k=\tfrac{a}{2}.$$ $$r^2=2\left(\tfrac{a}{2}\right)^2=\tfrac{a^2}{2}.$$ $$\therefore \left(x-\tfrac{a}{2}\right)^2+\left(y-\tfrac{a}{2}\right)^2=\tfrac{a^2}{2}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle through point with centre constrained by distance
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle is at distance $$5$$ from $$P(2,1)$$ and the circle passes through $$Q(6,4).$$ Find the possible circle equations.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre lies on circle }(x-2)^2+(y-1)^2=25\text{ and also must satisfy }CQ=CQ=r.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Let centre }C(h,k). Given (h-2)^2+(k-1)^2=25.$$ $$Circle passes through Q and has radius r=CQ=\sqrt{(6-h)^2+(4-k)^2}.$$ $$But also circle must pass through Q, which holds by definition. Infinitely many circles unless radius is fixed or another condition is given. Therefore not uniquely determined; family of circles with centres on (h-2)^2+(k-1)^2=25\text{ and equation }(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=(6-h)^2+(4-k)^2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with centre at intersection and given radius
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle is the intersection of $$x-3y=1$$ and $$2x+y=11.$$ The circle touches the line $$x=0.$$ Find the circle equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Solve for centre; radius is distance to }x=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find k so circle has integer radius

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Equation from two tangency points on axes
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle touches the axes at $$A(4,0)$$ and $$B(0,3).$$ Find its equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Tangency points imply radius lines perpendicular to axes, so centre is }(4,3).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Touching }x\text{-axis at }(4,0)\Rightarrow \text{centre has }x=4.$$ $$\text{Touching }y\text{-axis at }(0,3)\Rightarrow \text{centre has }y=3.$$ $$C(4,3).$$ $$r=3\text{ (to x-axis)}\Rightarrow r^2=9.$$ $$\therefore (x-4)^2+(y-3)^2=9.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle through origin with given centre y-coordinate

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find k so circle passes through a vertex of a triangle
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The triangle has vertices $$A(0,0),B(6,0),C(0,8).$$ The circle has diameter $$AB$$. Find the equation of the circle and determine whether $$C$$ lies on it.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Diameter endpoints give centre and radius; test point }C.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$C_0\left(3,0\right),\ r=3.$$ $$\Rightarrow (x-3)^2+y^2=9.$$ $$\text{Test }(0,8):\ 9+64=73\neq9\Rightarrow C\text{ is not on the circle.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle with centre constrained by equal distances
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centre of a circle is equidistant from $$A(1,2)$$ and $$B(9,6)$$ and lies on the line $$y=2x-1.$$ Find the equation of the circle if it passes through $$A.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Centre lies on perpendicular bisector of }AB\text{ and on }y=2x-1.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$M(5,4),\ m_{AB}=\tfrac{4}{8}=\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_\perp=-2.$$ $$\text{Bisector: }y-4=-2(x-5)\Rightarrow y=-2x+14.$$ $$\text{Intersect with }y=2x-1:\ 2x-1=-2x+14\Rightarrow4x=15\Rightarrow x=\tfrac{15}{4},\ y=\tfrac{13}{2}.$$ $$C\left(\tfrac{15}{4},\tfrac{13}{2}\right).$$ $$r^2=CA^2=\left(\tfrac{15}{4}-1\right)^2+\left(\tfrac{13}{2}-2\right)^2=\left(\tfrac{11}{4}\right)^2+\left(\tfrac{9}{2}\right)^2=\tfrac{121}{16}+\tfrac{81}{4}=\tfrac{445}{16}.$$ $$\therefore \left(x-\tfrac{15}{4}\right)^2+\left(y-\tfrac{13}{2}\right)^2=\tfrac{445}{16}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} - 2 x + y^{2} + 2 y - 7=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} - 10 x + y^{2} + 8 y - 8=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_1.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{If }S_1=0\text{ and }S_2=0\text{ are the circles, then any circle through their intersection points is }S_1+\lambda S_2=0.\ \text{Substitute the required centre to find }\lambda.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$S_1:\ x^{2} - 2 x + y^{2} + 2 y - 7=0,\quad S_2:\ x^{2} - 10 x + y^{2} + 8 y - 8=0.$$ $$\text{Required circle: }S_1+\lambda S_2=0.$$ $$\text{Substitute centre }(1,-1)\text{ into }S_1+\lambda S_2=0\text{ to find }\lambda.$$ $$S_1(1,-1)=-9,\quad S_2(1,-1)=-24.$$ $$-\,r_1^2+\lambda(d^2-r_2^2)=0\Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{r_1^2}{d^2-r_2^2}=\frac{9}{-24}=- \frac{3}{8}.$$ $$\text{So the required circle is }5 x^{2} + 14 x + 5 y^{2} - 8 y - 32=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} + 6 x + y^{2} + 2 y - 3=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} - 2 x + y^{2} - 8 y - 5=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} + 6 x + y^{2} + 8 y - 5=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} + 8 x + y^{2} - 6 y - 27=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} - 4 x + y^{2} + 2 y - 11=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} + 2 x + y^{2} - 2 y - 15=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} - 4 x + y^{2} - 10 y + 13=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} - 4 x + y^{2} - 2 y - 15=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} + 10 x + y^{2} - 2 y - 23=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} - 2 x + y^{2} + 6 y - 2=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} - 6 x + y^{2} - 2 y - 3=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} + 8 x + y^{2} - 2 y - 27=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} + 4 x + y^{2} - 2 y - 7=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} + 2 x + y^{2} + 10 y - 11=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} - 8 x + y^{2} + 8 y - 11=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} + 8 x + y^{2} + 2 y - 24=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} - 2 x + y^{2} + 4 y - 5=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} - 2 x + y^{2} - 6 y - 15=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} + 8 x + y^{2} - 6 y - 12=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} - 4 x + y^{2} - 2 y - 31=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_1.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{If }S_1=0\text{ and }S_2=0\text{ are the circles, then any circle through their intersection points is }S_1+\lambda S_2=0.\ \text{Substitute the required centre to find }\lambda.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$S_1:\ x^{2} + 8 x + y^{2} - 6 y - 12=0,\quad S_2:\ x^{2} - 4 x + y^{2} - 2 y - 31=0.$$ $$\text{Required circle: }S_1+\lambda S_2=0.$$ $$\text{Substitute centre }(-4,3)\text{ into }S_1+\lambda S_2=0\text{ to find }\lambda.$$ $$S_1(-4,3)=-25,\quad S_2(-4,3)=64.$$ $$-\,r_1^2+\lambda(d^2-r_2^2)=0\Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{r_1^2}{d^2-r_2^2}=\frac{25}{64}.$$ $$\text{So the required circle is }89 x^{2} + 688 x + 89 y^{2} - 486 y - 1039=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} - 6 x + y^{2} + 10 y - 3=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} + 10 x + y^{2} + 2 y - 27=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_2.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{If }S_1=0\text{ and }S_2=0\text{ are the circles, then any circle through their intersection points is }S_1+\lambda S_2=0.\ \text{Substitute the required centre to find }\lambda.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$S_1:\ x^{2} - 6 x + y^{2} + 10 y - 3=0,\quad S_2:\ x^{2} + 10 x + y^{2} + 2 y - 27=0.$$ $$\text{Required circle: }S_1+\lambda S_2=0.$$ $$\text{Substitute centre }(-5,-1)\text{ into }S_1+\lambda S_2=0\text{ to find }\lambda.$$ $$S_1(-5,-1)=19,\quad S_2(-5,-1)=-25.$$ $$ (d^2-r_1^2)+\lambda(-r_2^2)=0\Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{d^2-r_1^2}{r_2^2}=\frac{19}{25}.$$ $$\text{So the required circle is }44 x^{2} - 112 x + 44 y^{2} + 268 y - 183=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} - 4 x + y^{2} + 4 y - 20=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} + 10 x + y^{2} + 6 y - 3=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$S_1:\ x^{2} - 4 x + y^{2} + 4 y - 20=0,\quad S_2:\ x^{2} + 10 x + y^{2} + 6 y - 3=0.$$ $$\text{Required circle: }S_1+\lambda S_2=0.$$ $$\text{Substitute centre }(2,-2)\text{ into }S_1+\lambda S_2=0\text{ to find }\lambda.$$ $$S_1(2,-2)=-36,\quad S_2(2,-2)=-4.$$ $$-\,r_1^2+\lambda(d^2-r_2^2)=0\Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{r_1^2}{d^2-r_2^2}=\frac{36}{-4}=-9.$$ $$\text{So the required circle is }8 x^{2} + 94 x + 8 y^{2} + 50 y - 207=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$\text{Two circles intersect at points }A,B.\ \text{Circle }C_1:\ x^{2} + 2 x + y^{2} + 8 y - 8=0,\ \text{and }C_2:\ x^{2} - 2 x + y^{2} - 6 y - 11=0.$$ $$\text{Find the equation of the circle passing through }A,B\text{ and the centre of }C_2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$S_1:\ x^{2} + 2 x + y^{2} + 8 y - 8=0,\quad S_2:\ x^{2} - 2 x + y^{2} - 6 y - 11=0.$$ $$\text{Required circle: }S_1+\lambda S_2=0.$$ $$\text{Substitute centre }(1,3)\text{ into }S_1+\lambda S_2=0\text{ to find }\lambda.$$ $$S_1(1,3)=20,\quad S_2(1,3)=-16.$$ $$ (d^2-r_1^2)+\lambda(-r_2^2)=0\Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{d^2-r_1^2}{r_2^2}=\frac{20}{16}=\frac{5}{4}.$$ $$\text{So the required circle is }9 x^{2} + 2 x + 9 y^{2} + 14 y - 135=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Common points + centre on given line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$C_1:(x-1)^2+(y-4)^2=29,\ C_2:(x-6)^2+(y+1)^2=20,\ C_3:(x-3)^2+(y-1)^2=13\text{ intersect at the same two points }A,B.$$ $$\text{Find the circle through }A,B\text{ whose centre lies on }x+y=2.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$S_1:\ x^2+y^2-2x-8y-12=0,\ S_2:\ x^2+y^2-12x+2y+17=0.$$ $$S=S_1+\lambda S_2=0\Rightarrow (1+\lambda)(x^2+y^2)+(-2-12\lambda)x+(-8+2\lambda)y+(-12+17\lambda)=0.$$ $$\text{Divide by }(1+\lambda):\ D=\frac{-2-12\lambda}{1+\lambda},\ E=\frac{-8+2\lambda}{1+\lambda}.$$ $$\text{Centre }=\left(-\tfrac{D}{2},-\tfrac{E}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{2+12\lambda}{2(1+\lambda)},\frac{8-2\lambda}{2(1+\lambda)}\right).$$ $$x+y=2\Rightarrow \frac{2+12\lambda+8-2\lambda}{2(1+\lambda)}=2\Rightarrow \frac{10+10\lambda}{2(1+\lambda)}=2\Rightarrow \frac{10}{2}=2\Rightarrow 5=2\ (\text{contradiction}).$$ $$\therefore \text{No such circle exists.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$C_1:(x+1)^2+(y-3)^2=34,\ C_2:(x-5)^2+(y-1)^2=10,\ C_3:(x-2)^2+(y-2)^2=17\text{ intersect at common points }A,B.$$ $$\text{Find the circle through }A,B\text{ and }P(4,5).$$
$$C_1:(x-2)^2+(y-2)^2=20,\ C_2:(x-8)^2+(y-2)^2=25,\ C_3:(x-5)^2+(y-2)^2=9\text{ share intersection points }A,B.$$ $$\text{Find the circle through }A,B\text{ that is tangent to the }x\text{-axis.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$S_1:\ x^2+y^2-4x-4y-12=0,\quad S_2:\ x^2+y^2-16x-4y+43=0.$$ $$S=S_1+\lambda S_2=0.$$ $$\text{Divide by }(1+\lambda)\ (\lambda\neq-1):\ x^2+y^2+Dx+Ey+F=0,$$ $$D=\frac{-4-16\lambda}{1+\lambda},\ E=\frac{-4-4\lambda}{1+\lambda}=-4,\ F=\frac{-12+43\lambda}{1+\lambda}.$$ $$\text{Centre }(h,k)=\left(-\tfrac{D}{2},-\tfrac{E}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{4+16\lambda}{2(1+\lambda)},2\right).$$ $$k=2\Rightarrow \text{tangent to }x\text{-axis means }r=2.$$ $$r^2=h^2+k^2-F= h^2+4-F=4\Rightarrow F=h^2.$$ $$h=\frac{4+16\lambda}{2(1+\lambda)}=\frac{2+8\lambda}{1+\lambda}.$$ $$F=\frac{-12+43\lambda}{1+\lambda}=\left(\frac{2+8\lambda}{1+\lambda}\right)^2.$$ $$\text{Solve: }(-12+43\lambda)(1+\lambda)=(2+8\lambda)^2.$$ $$-12+31\lambda+43\lambda^2=4+32\lambda+64\lambda^2\Rightarrow 21\lambda^2+\lambda+16=0\Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{-1\pm i\sqrt{1343}}{42}.$$ $$\therefore \text{No real circle in the family is tangent to the }x\text{-axis.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: $$C_1:(x-4)^2+(y+1)^2=50,\ C_2:(x+2)^2+(y-3)^2=29,\ C_3:(x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=26\text{ share common points }A,B.$$ $$\text{Find the circle through }A,B\text{ and }P(0,2).$$
$$C_1:(x-3)^2+(y-4)^2=25,\ C_2:(x+1)^2+(y-2)^2=13,\ C_3:(x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=17\text{ intersect at the same two points }A,B.$$ $$\text{Find the circle through }A,B\text{ and }O(0,0).$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$S_1:\ x^2+y^2-6x-8y=0,\quad S_2:\ x^2+y^2+2x-4y-8=0.$$ $$O:\ S_1=0,\ S_2=-8\Rightarrow 0+\lambda(-8)=0\Rightarrow \lambda=0.$$ $$\text{Required circle is }S_1=0\Rightarrow x^2+y^2-6x-8y=0.$$

(b) Find the equation perpendicular bisector of line segment $$AB$$. (c) Show this bisector of AB passes through the circle’s centre. (d) Find the area of $$\triangle OAB$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use $$y=x-5$$ in the circle; midpoint–slope for bisector; check centre; area with base–height.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Substitute: $$(x-4)^2+(x+2)^2=50\Rightarrow2x^2-4x-30=0\Rightarrow x=5,-3.$$ Then $$y=x-5\Rightarrow A(5,0),\ B(-3,-8).$$ (b) $$M=\big(\tfrac{5+(-3)}{2},\tfrac{0+(-8)}{2}\big)=(1,-4),\ m_{AB}=1\Rightarrow m_\perp=-1,$$ so $$y+4=-1(x-1)\Rightarrow x+y+3=0.$$ (c) Centre $$C(4,-7):\ 4+(-7)+3=0\Rightarrow C$$ lies on the bisector. (d) Base $$OA=5$$ on the $$x$$-axis, height $$=|y_B|=8,$$ so $$\text{Area}=\tfrac12\cdot5\cdot8=\boxed{20}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x^2+2x+(4x-1)^2=k\Rightarrow 17x^2-6x+1-k=0.$$ $$\Delta=(-6)^2-4\cdot17(1-k)<0\Rightarrow36-68(1-k)<0\Rightarrow k<\tfrac{8}{17}.$$ Since a circle needs $$k>-1$$ (because $$(x+1)^2+y^2=k+1$$), range $$\boxed{-1<k<\tfrac{8}{17}}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$(x+1)^2+(y-2)^2=20$$ meets the line $$2x-y+5=0$$ at $$A,B.$$ Find $$A,B$$ and show $$AB$$ is a diameter.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Substitute line into circle; check line passes through centre.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$2x-y+5=0\Rightarrow y=2x+5.$$ Substitute: $$(x+1)^2+(2x+5-2)^2=20\Rightarrow(x+1)^2+(2x+3)^2=20.$$ $$x^2+2x+1+4x^2+12x+9=20\Rightarrow5x^2+14x-10=0.$$ $$x=\frac{-14\pm\sqrt{196+200}}{10}=\frac{-14\pm6\sqrt{11}}{10}=\frac{-7\pm3\sqrt{11}}{5}.$$ $$y=2x+5=\frac{11\pm6\sqrt{11}}{5}.$$ $$\text{Centre }(-1,2):\ 2(-1)-2+5=1\neq0\Rightarrow\text{line not through centre, so }AB\text{ not a diameter.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x^2+(mx+1)^2=10\Rightarrow(1+m^2)x^2+2mx-9=0.$$ $$\Delta=(2m)^2-4(1+m^2)(-9)=0\Rightarrow4m^2+36+36m^2=0\Rightarrow40m^2+36=0.$$ $$m^2=-\frac{9}{10}\Rightarrow\text{no real }m\text{, so no such tangent of form }y=mx+1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line $$y=2x$$ meets the circle $$x^2+y^2-4x-10y+13=0$$ at $$A,B.$$ Find the length $$AB.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x^2+4x^2-4x-20x+13=0\Rightarrow5x^2-24x+13=0.$$ $$x=\frac{24\pm\sqrt{576-260}}{10}=\frac{24\pm\sqrt{316}}{10}=\frac{12\pm\sqrt{79}}{5}.$$ $$\Delta x=\frac{2\sqrt{79}}{5}.$$ $$\text{Along line }y=2x,\ \Delta y=2\Delta x=\frac{4\sqrt{79}}{5}.$$ $$AB=\sqrt{(\Delta x)^2+(\Delta y)^2}=\Delta x\sqrt{1+4}=\frac{2\sqrt{79}}{5}\sqrt5=\frac{2\sqrt{395}}{5}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Show that the line $$x+2y-6=0$$ is tangent to the circle $$x^2+y^2-2x-4y+1=0.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Substitute and show quadratic has repeated root.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x+2y-6=0\Rightarrow x=6-2y.$$ Substitute: $$(6-2y)^2+y^2-2(6-2y)-4y+1=0.$$ $$36-24y+4y^2+y^2-12+4y-4y+1=0\Rightarrow5y^2-24y+25=0.$$ $$\Delta=(-24)^2-4\cdot5\cdot25=576-500=76\neq0\Rightarrow\text{not tangent.}$$ $$\text{Therefore the statement is false (it cuts at two points).}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2=25$$ meets the line $$y=4x-3$$ at $$A,B.$$ Find the equation of the line through $$A,B$$ with gradient $$-1$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Find midpoint of chord using perpendicular from centre; then use point-slope with gradient }-1.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Chord }AB\text{ lies on }y=4x-3\Rightarrow4x-y-3=0.$$ $$\text{Midpoint }M\text{ is foot from }O(0,0):\ y=\tfrac14x-\tfrac34\ (\text{perp slope }=\tfrac14).$$ $$\text{Intersect: }4x-(\tfrac14x-\tfrac34)-3=0\Rightarrow \tfrac{15}{4}x-\tfrac{9}{4}=0\Rightarrow x=\tfrac35,\ y=4(\tfrac35)-3=-\tfrac35.$$ $$\text{Line with slope }-1\text{ through }M:\ y+\tfrac35=-1(x-\tfrac35)\Rightarrow x+y=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.subtopic_name: Intersections of straight lines and circles

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line $$y=k$$ cuts the circle $$x^2+y^2-4x=0$$ at $$A,B.$$ Express $$AB$$ in terms of $$k$$ and state when it is real.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x^2+k^2-4x=0\Rightarrow x^2-4x+k^2=0\Rightarrow x=2\pm\sqrt{4-k^2}.$$ $$AB=\Delta x=2\sqrt{4-k^2}.$$ $$\text{Real iff }4-k^2\ge0\Rightarrow -2\le k\le2,\ \text{and distinct if }|k|<2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x^2+y^2-8y-9=0\Rightarrow x^2+(y-4)^2=25.$$ $$\text{Centre }(0,4),\ r=5.$$ $$\text{Line }px-y+4=0,\ d=\frac{|p\cdot0-4+4|}{\sqrt{p^2+1}}=0.$$ $$d=0<5\Rightarrow \text{line passes through centre, so it is not tangent for any real }p.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.subtopic_name: Intersections of straight lines and circles
Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Hard composite: intersections, chord bisector, area
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Circle $$x^2+y^2-6x-8y+9=0$$ meets line $$2x+y-4=0$$ at $$A,B.$$ (a) Find $$A,B.$$ (b) Find equation of perpendicular bisector of $$AB.$$ (c) Find area of $$\triangle OAB$$ where $$O$$ is circle centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{(a) substitute; (b) midpoint+slope; (c) base }AB\text{ and height from centre to chord.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Circle: }(x-3)^2+(y-4)^2=16,\ O(3,4),\ r=4.$$ $$(a)\ y=4-2x.$$ $$(x-3)^2+(4-2x-4)^2=16\Rightarrow(x-3)^2+4x^2=16\Rightarrow5x^2-6x-7=0.$$ $$x=\frac{6\pm\sqrt{36+140}}{10}=\frac{6\pm4\sqrt{11}}{10}=\frac{3\pm2\sqrt{11}}{5}.$$ $$y=4-2x=\frac{14\mp4\sqrt{11}}{5}.$$ $$(b)\ m_{AB}=-2\Rightarrow m_\perp=\tfrac12.$$ Midpoint $$M=(3,4)=O,$$ so bisector is $$y-4=\tfrac12(x-3)\Rightarrow x-2y+5=0.$$ $$(c)\ \text{Chord distance }d=\frac{|2\cdot3+4-4|}{\sqrt{2^2+1^2}}=\frac{6}{\sqrt5}.$$ $$AB=2\sqrt{r^2-d^2}=2\sqrt{16-\frac{36}{5}}=2\sqrt{\frac{44}{5}}=\frac{4\sqrt{55}}{5}.$$ $$\text{Area}=\tfrac12\cdot AB\cdot d=\tfrac12\cdot\frac{4\sqrt{55}}{5}\cdot\frac{6}{\sqrt5}=\frac{12\sqrt{11}}{5}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Tangent from a variable point on a line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Point $$P(t,1)$$ lies on the line $$y=1$$. The tangent(s) from $$P$$ to the circle $$x^2+y^2=9$$ exist for some values of $$t$$. (a) Find the condition on $$t$$ for tangents to exist. (b) For those $$t$$, find the equation(s) of the tangent line(s).
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$(a)\ OP^2=t^2+1^2=t^2+1.\ \text{Tangents exist iff }OP>3\Rightarrow t^2+1>9\Rightarrow t^2>8.$$ $$\Rightarrow t<-2\sqrt2\ \text{or}\ t>2\sqrt2.$$ $$(b)\ \text{Line: }y-1=m(x-t)\Rightarrow mx-y+(1-mt)=0.$$ $$\text{Distance from }O(0,0):\ \frac{|1-mt|}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}=3.$$ $$\Rightarrow(1-mt)^2=9(m^2+1)\Rightarrow t^2m^2-2tm+1=9m^2+9.$$ $$\Rightarrow (t^2-9)m^2-2tm-8=0.$$ $$m=\frac{2t\pm\sqrt{4t^2+32(t^2-9)}}{2(t^2-9)}=\frac{2t\pm\sqrt{36t^2-288}}{2(t^2-9)}=\frac{t\pm3\sqrt{t^2-8}}{t^2-9}.$$ $$\text{Tangents: }y-1=\left(\frac{t\pm3\sqrt{t^2-8}}{t^2-9}\right)(x-t).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.subtopic_name: Intersections of straight lines and circles
Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Chord midpoint path under parallel lines
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle is $$x^2+y^2=25$$. For real $$c$$, the line $$y=2x+c$$ cuts the circle in chord $$AB$$. Find the locus of the midpoint of $$AB$$ as $$c$$ varies.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Midpoint is foot of perpendicular from centre to the chord line.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Circle centre }O(0,0). \text{Chord line }2x-y+c=0.$$ $$\text{Foot from origin to }ax+by+c=0\text{ is }\left(\frac{-ac}{a^2+b^2},\frac{-bc}{a^2+b^2}\right).$$ $$a=2,b=-1\Rightarrow M\left(\frac{-2c}{5},\frac{c}{5}\right).$$ $$\text{Eliminate }c:\ x=-2y.$$ $$\therefore \text{locus is }x+2y=0.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$C(2,1).$$ $$\overrightarrow{CM}=(2,2)\Rightarrow m_{CM}=1.$$ $$\text{Chord line has slope }1\Rightarrow \text{but }y=x+c\text{ also slope }1,\ \text{so }CM\parallel AB\text{ not }\perp.$$ $$\text{This contradicts chord property, so no such }c\text{ exists.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.subtopic_name: Intersections of straight lines and circles
Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Distance between intersections in closed form
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line $$y=mx+4$$ meets the circle $$x^2+y^2=25$$ at points $$A,B$$ (if it intersects). Derive a formula for $$AB$$ in terms of $$m$$ and state the condition for real intersections.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Line }mx-y+4=0,\ d=\frac{4}{\sqrt{m^2+1}},\ r=5.$$ $$AB=2\sqrt{25-\frac{16}{m^2+1}}=2\sqrt{\frac{25(m^2+1)-16}{m^2+1}}=2\sqrt{\frac{25m^2+9}{m^2+1}}.$$ $$\text{Real intersections iff }d\le r\Rightarrow \frac{4}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}\le5\Rightarrow m^2+1\ge\frac{16}{25}\ \text{always true.}$$ $$\text{Distinct iff }d<r\Rightarrow m^2+1>\frac{16}{25}\ \text{always, so always two points.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.subtopic_name: Intersections of straight lines and circles

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: All lines through $$P(0,4)$$ cut the circle $$x^2+y^2=16$$ in chords. Show that the product of distances from $$P$$ to the two intersection points is constant and find it.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Use power of a point with respect to circle centred at origin.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Circle centre }O(0,0),\ r^2=16.$$ $$OP^2=0^2+4^2=16.$$ $$\text{Power of }P:\ OP^2-r^2=16-16=0.$$ $$\therefore PA\cdot PB=0\text{ for any secant through }P,\ \text{meaning every such line meets the circle with }P\text{ itself as a point of contact/intersection.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Intersection coordinates then area with centre
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Circle $$(x-4)^2+(y+1)^2=50$$ meets line $$x-y-5=0$$ at $$A,B.$$ Find $$A,B$$ and the area of $$\triangle CAB$$ where $$C$$ is the centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$y=x-5\Rightarrow(x-4)^2+(x-5+1)^2=50\Rightarrow(x-4)^2+(x-4)^2=50.$$ $$2(x-4)^2=50\Rightarrow x-4=\pm5\Rightarrow x=9,-1.$$ $$y=x-5\Rightarrow A(9,4),\ B(-1,-6).$$ $$C(4,-1),\ r=\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt2.$$ $$\text{Chord length }AB=\sqrt{(10)^2+(10)^2}=10\sqrt2.$$ $$\text{Distance }d=\text{dist}(C,\ x-y-5=0)=\frac{|4-(-1)-5|}{\sqrt2}=0.$$ $$\text{So line passes through centre, chord is diameter; area }=\tfrac12\cdot AB\cdot0=0\text{ (degenerate since }C\text{ lies on }AB).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line $$y=mx+1$$ cuts the circle $$x^2+y^2=10$$ in chord $$AB$$ whose midpoint is $$M(1,2).$$ Find $$m.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{For circle centred at origin, midpoint is foot from origin to the chord line.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Chord line }mx-y+1=0.$$ $$\text{Foot from origin to }ax+by+c=0\text{ is }\left(\frac{-ac}{a^2+b^2},\frac{-bc}{a^2+b^2}\right).$$ $$a=m,b=-1,c=1\Rightarrow M\left(\frac{-m}{m^2+1},\frac{1}{m^2+1}\right)=(1,2).$$ $$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{m^2+1}=2\Rightarrow m^2+1=\tfrac12\Rightarrow m^2=-\tfrac12.$$ $$\text{No real }m.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.subtopic_name: Intersections of straight lines and circles
Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Find k so the line passes through both intersections of circles
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circles $$x^2+y^2=13$$ and $$x^2+y^2-4x+6y-3=0$$ intersect at $$A,B.$$ Find the equation of line $$AB$$ and hence find $$k$$ such that $$y=kx+1$$ passes through both points.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Line }AB\text{ is radical axis; then compare form.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Subtract: }(x^2+y^2)-(x^2+y^2-4x+6y-3)=13-0\Rightarrow4x-6y+3=13.$$ $$\Rightarrow4x-6y-10=0\Rightarrow2x-3y-5=0.$$ $$\text{This is not of the form }y=kx+1\text{ unless it can be rearranged to }y=kx+1.$$ $$2x-3y-5=0\Rightarrow y=\tfrac23x-\tfrac53\Rightarrow \text{intercept is }-\tfrac53\neq1.$$ $$\therefore \text{no such }k\text{ exists.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.subtopic_name: Intersections of straight lines and circles
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line $$y=x+c$$ cuts $$x^2+y^2=25$$ in chord $$AB$$. The line $$y=-x+c$$ cuts the circle in chord $$CD$$. Find $$c$$ such that chords $$AB$$ and $$CD$$ have equal length.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Equal chord lengths ⇔ equal distance from centre. Use distances from origin to lines.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$d_{AB}=\frac{|c|}{\sqrt2},\ d_{CD}=\frac{|c|}{\sqrt2}\Rightarrow d_{AB}=d_{CD}\ \text{always}.$$ $$\Rightarrow \text{Chord lengths are equal for all real }c\text{ with intersection.}$$ $$\text{Intersection requires }d<5\Rightarrow \frac{|c|}{\sqrt2}<5\Rightarrow |c|<5\sqrt2.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2-2x+4y-20=0$$ meets the line $$y=2$$ at $$A,B.$$ Find the equation of chord $$AB$$ and its perpendicular bisector.

Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$x^2+(2)^2-2x+8-20=0\Rightarrow x^2-2x-8=0\Rightarrow x=4,-2.$$ $$A(4,2),B(-2,2),\ AB:\ y=2.$$ $$\text{Centre: }(1,-2). \ \text{Perp bisector is vertical through midpoint }M(1,2):\ x=1.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.subtopic_name: Intersections of straight lines and circles
Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Secant through fixed point with fixed chord length
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle is $$x^2+y^2=25.$$ A line through $$P(0,1)$$ cuts the circle in chord $$AB$$ of length $$8.$$ Find the possible equations of the line.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Use }AB=2\sqrt{r^2-d^2}\Rightarrow d=3,\ \text{then find lines through }P\text{ at distance }3\text{ from origin.}$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$r=5,\ 8=2\sqrt{25-d^2}\Rightarrow d^2=9\Rightarrow d=3.$$ $$\text{Let line through }P:\ y=mx+1\Rightarrow mx-y+1=0.$$ $$\text{Distance from origin }d=\frac{|1|}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}=3\Rightarrow \sqrt{m^2+1}=\tfrac13\Rightarrow m^2=-\tfrac{8}{9}.$$ $$\text{No real }m,\ \therefore \text{no such line exists.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2+y^2-6x+4y-12=0$$ has tangents at points $$P,Q$$ lying on the line $$y=x$$. Find the midpoint of chord $$PQ$$.

Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Centre }(3,-2).$$ $$PQ:y=x\Rightarrow m=1.$$ $$\text{Perpendicular line slope }=-1.$$ $$\text{Midpoint lies on }y+2=-1(x-3)\Rightarrow x+y-1=0.$$ $$\text{Intersect with }y=x\Rightarrow (x,y)=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$ (x-2)^2+(y-3)^2=13$$. A tangent is drawn from $$A(5,0)$$. Find the equation(s) of the tangent(s).
