The tangents at $$P,Q$$ to a circle meet at $$A$$. Show that $$A$$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $$PQ$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$AP=AQ\Rightarrow A\text{ lies on perpendicular bisector of }PQ.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has centre $$P(-2,4)$$ and passes through $$Q(4,0)$$. (a) Find the equation of the circle. (b) Find the equation of the tangent at $$Q$$. (c) A line parallel to this tangent passes through the midpoint of $$PQ$$ and meets the circle at $$A,B$$. Find $$AB$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Radius }PQ;\ \text{tangent }\perp PQ;\ \text{distance of parallel chord from centre}. $$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$(a)\ r^2=(6)^2+(-4)^2=52\Rightarrow (x+2)^2+(y-4)^2=52.$$ $$(b)\ m_{PQ}=-\tfrac{4}{6}=-\tfrac23\Rightarrow m_{\tan}=\tfrac32,$$ $$y=\tfrac32(x-4).$$ $$(c)\ M(1,2),\ \text{distance from centre}= \sqrt5.$$ $$AB=2\sqrt{52-5}=2\sqrt{47}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle from tangent point and centre
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has centre $$C(5,-1)$$ and tangent $$3x+4y-17=0$$ touches the circle at $$T$$. (a) Find the equation of the circle. (b) Find $$T$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Perpendicular distance gives radius; foot of perpendicular gives }T.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$ (x-3)^2+(y+2)^2=25$$ has tangent at $$Q(8,-2)$$. A chord parallel to the tangent passes through the midpoint of $$CQ$$. Find the chord length.
The tangents at $$P,Q$$ to the circle $$ (x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=10$$ meet at $$A(5,7)$$. Find the midpoint of $$PQ$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Midpoint lies on line joining }A\text{ and centre}. $$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The tangents from $$A(7,3)$$ to the circle $$ (x-2)^2+(y-1)^2=13$$ touch at $$P,Q$$. Find the equation of chord $$PQ$$.
The tangent at $$Q(6,4)$$ to the circle $$ (x-2)^2+(y-4)^2=16$$ is drawn. A second tangent parallel to it cuts the circle in chord $$AB$$. Find $$AB$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Distance between parallel tangents determines chord length}. $$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The tangent to the circle $$ (x-4)^2+(y-1)^2=20$$ has slope $$-2$$. Find the point of contact.
The tangent at $$Q(3,7)$$ to the circle $$ (x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=20$$ is drawn. A chord parallel to this tangent is 4 units from the centre. Find its length.
The tangent at $$Q(5,1)$$ to the circle $$ (x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=16$$ meets the diameter through $$Q$$ at $$T$$. Find $$QT$$.
The tangents at $$P,Q$$ to the circle $$ (x-2)^2+(y-2)^2=8$$ meet at $$A(6,6)$$. Find the area of $$\triangle APQ$$.
The tangent from the y-axis to the circle $$ (x-3)^2+(y-2)^2=10$$ touches at $$P$$. Find $$P$$.
The tangent at $$Q$$ to the circle $$ (x+2)^2+(y-1)^2=29$$ has slope $$1$$. A parallel chord has length $$6$$. Find its distance from the centre.
Show that the tangents at the endpoints of a diameter of a circle meet on the perpendicular through the centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$\text{Tangents are parallel; intersection at infinity or perpendicular alignment proven}. $$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The tangent from the origin to the circle $$ (x-5)^2+(y-4)^2=41$$ touches at $$P$$. Find $$P$$.
The chord of contact from $$A(8,6)$$ to the circle $$ (x-3)^2+(y-2)^2=20$$ has midpoint $$M$$. Find $$M$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: $$\text{Midpoint lies on line joining }A\text{ and centre}. $$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The tangent to $$ (x-1)^2+(y-2)^2=13$$ is shifted 3 units towards the centre. Find the new chord length.
The tangents from $$A(7,1)$$ to the circle $$ (x-2)^2+(y-1)^2=9$$ touch at $$P,Q$$. Find the perimeter of $$\triangle APQ$$.
Show that the line joining the centre of a circle to the intersection of tangents at $$P,Q$$ bisects angle $$PAQ$$.
The tangent at $$Q(7,3)$$ to the circle $$ (x-3)^2+(y-3)^2=25$$ is drawn. A chord parallel to it is at distance 4 from the centre. Find its length.
The circle has centre $$C(4,-1)$$ and tangent $$2x-y-5=0$$. A chord parallel to this tangent passes through $$C$$. Find its endpoints.
The line $$x+3y-11=0$$ touches the circle $$(x+1)^2+(y+6)^2=r^2$$ at $$(2,3)$$. (a) Find the radius of circle. (b) Show the radius at $$(2,3)$$ is perpendicular to the line.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: (a) Radius is distance from centre $$(-1,-6)$$ to $$(2,3)$$. (b) Compare slopes of the radius and the line.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$r=\sqrt{(2+1)^2+(3+6)^2}=\sqrt{9+81}=3\sqrt{10}.$$ (b) Radius slope $$m_r=\tfrac{3-(-6)}{2-(-1)}=\tfrac{9}{3}=3$$; line slope from $$x+3y-11=0$$ is $$m_\ell=-\tfrac13.$$ Since $$m_rm_\ell=-1,$$ they are perpendicular.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The point $$P(1,-2)$$ lies on the circle with centre $$(4,6)$$. (a) Find the equation of the circle. (b) Find the equation of the tangent at $$P$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: (a) Use $$r^2=|CP|^2.$$ (b) Tangent slope is negative reciprocal of radius slope.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The Points A and B with coordinates  $$(-1,-9),(7,-5)$$ lie on circle $$C:(x-1)^2+(y+3)^2=40.$$ (a) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the line segment $$AB$$. (b) Show that the perpendicular of bisector $$AB$$ passes through the centre of $$C$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Midpoint+slope for $$AB$$; perpendicular slope; check centre $$(1,-3)$$ lies on the line.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$M(3,-7),\,m_{AB}=\tfrac{4}{8}=\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_\perp=-2.$$ $$y+7=-2(x-3)\Rightarrow \boxed{2x+y+1=0}.$$ (b) Centre $$(1,-3)$$ gives $$2(1)+(-3)+1=0,$$ so the line passes through the centre.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The Points P and Q with coordinates $$(3,1),(5,-3)$$ lie on the circle $$x^2-4x+y^2+4y=2.$$ (a) Find the perpendicular bisector of $$PQ$$. (b)Show that the perpendicular of bisector $$PQ$$ passes through the centre of $$C$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Complete square for centre; compute bisector via midpoint+slope.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$M(4,-1),\,m_{PQ}=-2\Rightarrow m_\perp=\tfrac12.$$ $$y+1=\tfrac12(x-4)\Rightarrow \boxed{x-2y-6=0}.$$ (b) Circle $$(x-2)^2+(y+2)^2=10$$ has centre $$(2,-2).$$ Sub: $$2-2(-2)-6=0,$$ so centre lies on the bisector.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The Circle has the equation $$ x^2+18x+y^2-2y+29=0.$$ (a) Verify $$P(-7,-6)$$ lies on $$C$$. (b) Find an equation of the tangent to $$C$$ at $$P$$ in the form $$y=mx+b$$. (c) Find the coordinates of $$R,$$ the intersection of this tangent with the $$y$$-axis. (d) Find the area of $$\triangle APR,$$ where $$A$$ is the centre of $$C$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Complete squares for centre; use radius–tangent perpendicularity; for (d) use area $$\tfrac12|x_A(y_P-y_R)+x_P(y_R-y_A)+x_R(y_A-y_P)|$$ or vector determinant.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$49-126+36+12+29=0\Rightarrow P\in C.$$ (b) $$(x+9)^2+(y-1)^2=53\Rightarrow A(-9,1).$$ Radius slope $$=\tfrac{-6-1}{-7-(-9)}=-\tfrac72\Rightarrow m_t=\tfrac{2}{7}.$$ Tangent: $$y+6=\tfrac{2}{7}(x+7)\Rightarrow \boxed{y=\tfrac{2}{7}x-4}.$$ (c) Set $$x=0\Rightarrow R(0,-4).$$ (d) $$A(-9,1),P(-7,-6),R(0,-4).$$ Area $$=\tfrac12|\,\det(\overrightarrow{AP},\overrightarrow{AR})\,|=\tfrac12|\,\langle2,-7\rangle\times\langle9,-5\rangle\,|=\tfrac12|(-10+63)|=\boxed{\tfrac{53}{2}}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The tangent to the circle $$(x+4)^2+(y-1)^2=242$$ at $$(7,-10)$$ meets the $$y$$-axis at $$S$$ and the $$x$$-axis at $$T$$. (a) Find $$S,T$$. (b) Hence find the area of $$\triangle OST$$ where $$O$$ is the origin.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find tangent eqn using point–radius perpendicularity, then find intercepts.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Centre $$(-4,1)$$; radius slope $$=\tfrac{-10-1}{7+4}=-1.$$ Hence tangent slope $$=1$$. Through $$(7,-10): y+10=1(x-7)\Rightarrow y=x-17.$$ For $$S$$: $$x=0\Rightarrow y=-17\Rightarrow S(0,-17);$$ for $$T$$: $$y=0\Rightarrow x=17\Rightarrow T(17,0).$$ (b) Area $$=\tfrac12|x_Ty_S-x_Sy_T|=\tfrac12(17\times17)=\boxed{144.5}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Circle $$C:(x+5)^2+(y+3)^2=80.$$ Line $$l$$ is tangent with gradient 2. Find the two possible equations of $$l$$ in $$y=mx+c$$ form.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Distance from circle centre to line $$=r$$; solve for $$c$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Radius $$r=\sqrt{80}=4\sqrt5,\,$$ centre $$(-5,-3).$$ For $$y=2x+c$$, distance $$=\dfrac{|2(-5)-(-3)+c|}{\sqrt{1+2^2}}=\dfrac{|c-(-10+3)|}{\sqrt5}=\dfrac{|c+7|}{\sqrt5}=4\sqrt5\Rightarrow |c+7|=20.$$ Hence $$\boxed{y=2x+13\text{ or }y=2x-27.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line $$2x+y-5=0$$ is tangent to the circle $$(x-3)^2+(y-p)^2=5.$$ (a) Find both possible $$p$$. (b) Write down each circle’s centre.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use distance from line to circle centre $$=r=\sqrt5.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Centre $$(3,p),$$ so distance $$=\dfrac{|2(3)+p-5|}{\sqrt5}=\dfrac{|p+1|}{\sqrt5}=\sqrt5\Rightarrow |p+1|=5.$$ Hence $$p=4$$ or $$p=-6.$$ (b) Centres $$\boxed{(3,4)}$$ and $$\boxed{(3,-6)}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$C$$ has centre $$P(11,-5)$$ and passes through $$Q(5,3)$$. (a) Find the equation of $$C$$. (b) The line $$l_1$$ is tangent to $$C$$ at $$Q$$ — find its equation. (c) The line $$l_2$$ is parallel to $$l_1$$ and passes through the midpoint of $$PQ$$; it meets $$C$$ at $$A,B$$. Find the coordinates of $$A,B$$. (d) Find the length $$AB$$ in simplest surd form.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use distance formula for radius; tangent ⟂ radius; parallel line through midpoint; intersection via substitution; distance formula for $$AB$$.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle from two points (line through centre)
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$R(2,3)$$ and $$S(10,1)$$ lie on a circle with centre $$C(a,-2)$$. Let $$M$$ be the midpoint of $$RS$$. The line $$l$$ passes through $$M$$ and $$C$$. (a) Find an equation of $$l$$. (b) Find the value of $$a$$. (c) Find the equation of the circle. (d) Find the points of intersection, $$A$$ and $$B$$, of the line $$l$$ and the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use midpoint for $$M$$; slope of $$MC$$ for $$l$$; set $$CR=CS$$ to get $$a$$; circle $$(x-a)^2+(y+2)^2=r^2$$ with $$r^2=CR^2$$; substitute $$l$$ into circle for $$A,B$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$M(6,2),\ C(a,-2)\Rightarrow m=\dfrac{-2-2}{a-6}=\dfrac{-4}{a-6};\ \text{with }a=5\Rightarrow m=4,\ l:\ y-2=4(x-6)\iff y=4x-22.$$ (b) $$CR^2=CS^2\Rightarrow(2-a)^2+5^2=(10-a)^2+3^2\Rightarrow a=5.$$ (c) $$r^2=(2-5)^2+(3+2)^2=34\Rightarrow (x-5)^2+(y+2)^2=34.$$ (d) Solve $$y=4x-22$$ with circle: $$x=5\pm\sqrt2,\ y=-2\pm4\sqrt2;$$ so $$A\!\left(5+\sqrt2,\,-2+4\sqrt2\right),\ B\!\left(5-\sqrt2,\,-2-4\sqrt2\right).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$x^2-4x+y^2-6y=7$$ and the line $$\ell:\ x-3y+17=0$$ meet at points $$P,Q$$. (a) Find the coordinates of $$P,Q$$. (b) Find equations of the tangents at $$P,Q$$. (c) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of chord $$PQ$$. (d) Show the two tangents and this bisector meet at one point, and find it.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Complete the square to get centre/radius; substitute line into circle for $$P,Q$$; tangent at a point is ⟂ to the radius; bisector passes through the midpoint and is ⟂ to chord (equivalently, passes through centre).
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$(x-2)^2+(y-3)^2=20,\ \ y=\tfrac{x+17}{3}.$$ Sub: $$(x-2)^2+\big(\tfrac{x+8}{3}\big)^2=20\Rightarrow x^2-2x-8=0\Rightarrow x\in\{4,-2\}.$$ Hence $$P(4,7),\ Q(-2,5).$$ (b) Centre $$C(2,3).$$ Slope $$CP=2\Rightarrow m_{\text{tan at }P}=-\tfrac12:\ \boxed{x+2y-18=0}.$$ Slope $$CQ=-\tfrac12\Rightarrow m_{\text{tan at }Q}=2:\ \boxed{2x-y+9=0}.$$ (c) Midpoint $$M(1,6),\ m_{PQ}=\tfrac{2}{6}=\tfrac13\Rightarrow m_{\perp}=-3:\ \boxed{3x+y-9=0}.$$ (d) Intersection of tangents: solve $$\begin{cases}x+2y-18=0\\[2pt]2x-y+9=0\end{cases}\Rightarrow (x,y)=(0,9).$$ Check on bisector: $$3\cdot0+9-9=0$$ so all three meet at $$\boxed{(0,9)}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Tangent through a given point (positive slope)
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle C has the equation $$(x-7)^2+(y+1)^2=5$$. A tangent line with positive gradient passes through $$(0,-2)$$. Find its equation in the form $$y=mx+c$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use $$c=-2$$ (passes through $$(0,-2)$$). For $$y=mx-2$$, the distance from centre $$(7,-1)$$ to the line must equal the radius $$\sqrt5$$.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle with centre $$C(2,1)$$ has equation $$(x-2)^2+(y-1)^2=10$$. Tangents at points $$P,Q$$ meet at $$R(6,-1)$$. (a) Show that $$CPRQ$$ is a square.(b) Hence find the equations of the tangents at $$P$$ and $$Q$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: (a) Use tangent-length and right-angle facts: $$RP=RQ=\sqrt{RC^2-r^2}$$ and radius $$\perp$$ tangent at contact. (b) Write line through $$R(6,-1)$$ as $$y+1=m(x-6)$$ and set distance from $$C(2,1)$$ to this line equal to $$\sqrt{10}$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Here $$RC^2=(6-2)^2+(-1-1)^2=20,\ r^2=10\Rightarrow RP=RQ=\sqrt{10}.$$ Also $$CP=CQ=\sqrt{10}$$ (radii) and $$CP\perp RP,\ CQ\perp RQ$$, so the four sides $$CP,PR,RQ,QC$$ are equal with a right angle ⇒ $$CPRQ$$ is a square. (b)For $$mx-y-6m-1=0$$, $$\dfrac{|2m-1-6m-1|}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}=\sqrt{10}\Rightarrow(4m+2)^2=10(m^2+1)\Rightarrow 3m^2+8m-3=0$$ giving $$m=\tfrac13$$ or $$m=-3$$. Hence tangents $$\boxed{y=\tfrac13x-3}$$ and $$\boxed{y=-3x+17}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$U(-2,8),\ V(7,7),\ W(-3,-1)$$ lie on a circle. (a) Show that triangle $$UVW$$ has a right angle. (b) find the coordinates of the centre of the circle. (c) Write down an equation of the circle through $$U,V,W$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: (a) Use squared side lengths and Pythagoras. (b) Right triangle ⇒ centre is midpoint of hypotenuse $$VW$$. (c) Use centre from (d) and $$r^2=CV^2$$.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$A(2,6),\ B(5,7),\ C(8,-2),$$ lie on a circle. (a) show that $$AC$$ is a diameter of the circle. (b) Write down an equation of the circle. (c) Find the area of triangle $$ABC$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: (a) Check $$\overline{AB}\perp\overline{CB}$$ (right angle at $$B$$). (b) Centre is midpoint of $$AC$$; $$r=\tfrac12|AC|$$. (c) Right triangle at $$B$$ ⇒ $$\tfrac12\cdot|AB|\cdot|BC|$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$m_{AB}=\tfrac{1}{3},\ m_{CB}=-3,\ m_{AB}m_{CB}=-1\Rightarrow\angle ABC=90^\circ.$$ Hence $$AC$$ is a diameter. (b) $$C_0=\big(\tfrac{2+8}{2},\tfrac{6+(-2)}{2}\big)=(5,2),\ r^2=(2-5)^2+(6-2)^2=25.$$ So $$(x-5)^2+(y-2)^2=25.$$ (c) $$|AB|=\sqrt{10},\ |BC|=\sqrt{90}=3\sqrt{10}\Rightarrow\text{Area}=\tfrac12(\sqrt{10})(3\sqrt{10})=15.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: (a) The points $$A(-3,19),\ B(9,11),\ C(-15,1)$$ lie on a circle. (i) Find the perpendicular bisector of $$AB$$.(ii) Find the perpendicular bisector of $$AC$$. (b) Find the centre of the circle and (c) write its equation.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Midpoint–slope, then negative reciprocal.Intersect the two bisectors; then use $$r^2=CA^2$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) (i) $$M_{AB}(3,15),\ m_{AB}=-\tfrac{2}{3}\Rightarrow m_\perp=\tfrac{3}{2}.$$ $$y-15=\tfrac{3}{2}(x-3)\Rightarrow \boxed{3x-2y+21=0}.$$ (ii) $$M_{AC}(-9,10),\ m_{AC}=\tfrac{3}{2}\Rightarrow m_\perp=-\tfrac{2}{3}.$$ $$y-10=-\tfrac{2}{3}(x+9)\Rightarrow \boxed{2x+3y-12=0}.$$ (b) Intersecting $$3x-2y+21=0$$ and $$2x+3y-12=0$$ by solving the equation $$x,y$$ is $$(-3,6)$$. So the centre is $$(-3,6)$$ (c) $$r^2=( -3-(-3))^2+(19-6)^2=169.$$ So the equation is $$(x+3)^2+(y-6)^2=169.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Find the perpendicular bisector of (i) $$PQ$$ and (ii) $$QR$$ for the points $$P(-11,8),~Q(-6,-7),~R(4,-7)$$ on a circle, and hence (b) find an equation of the circle through $$P,Q,R$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: For each chord: find midpoint and slope $$m=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$$, then perpendicular slope $$m_\perp=-\frac{1}{m}$$. Intersect bisectors to find the centre; use $$r^2=(x-x_c)^2+(y-y_c)^2$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (i) For $$PQ$$: $$M_{PQ}\Big(\frac{-11-6}{2},\frac{8+(-7)}{2}\Big)=\Big(-\frac{17}{2},\frac{1}{2}\Big),\ m_{PQ}=\frac{-7-8}{-6-(-11)}=-3 \Rightarrow m_\perp=\frac{1}{3}.$$ Hence $$y-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{3}\left(x+\frac{17}{2}\right)\Rightarrow 3y=x+10\Rightarrow \boxed{x-3y+10=0}.$$ (ii) For $$QR$$: $$M_{QR}=\Big(\frac{-6+4}{2},\frac{-7-7}{2}\Big)=(-1,-7),~m_{QR}=0\Rightarrow \text{bisector is vertical: }\boxed{x=-1}.$$ (b) Centre at intersection $$x=-1,~x-3y+10=0\Rightarrow y=3,$$ so $$C(-1,3).$$ Radius squared $$r^2=CP^2=(-1+11)^2+(3-8)^2=10^2+(-5)^2=125.$$ Thus the circle is $$\boxed{(x+1)^2+(y-3)^2=125}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$R(-2,1),~S(4,3),~T(10,-5)$$ lie on a circle $$C$$. Find the equation of $$C$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use perpendicular bisectors of chords $$RS$$ and $$ST$$; their intersection gives the centre, and $$r^2$$ follows from any point.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Chord $$RS$$: midpoint $$M_{RS}(1,2),~m_{RS}=\frac{3-1}{4-(-2)}=\frac{1}{3}\Rightarrow m_\perp=-3.$$ Equation: $$y-2=-3(x-1)\Rightarrow 3x+y-5=0.$$ Chord $$ST$$: midpoint $$M_{ST}(7,-1),~m_{ST}=\frac{-5-3}{10-4}=-\frac{4}{3}\Rightarrow m_\perp=\frac{3}{4}.$$ Equation: $$y+1=\frac{3}{4}(x-7)\Rightarrow 3x-4y-25=0.$$ Intersection of $$3x+y-5=0$$ and $$3x-4y-25=0$$ gives $$x=3,~y=-4.$$ Hence centre $$C(3,-4)$$ and $$r^2=(3+2)^2+(-4-1)^2=5^2+(-5)^2=50.$$ Thus $$\boxed{(x-3)^2+(y+4)^2=50}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Consider points $$A(3,15),~B(-13,3),~C(-7,-5),~D(8,0).$$ (a) Show $$\triangle ABC$$ is right-angled. (b) Find the equation of the circumcircle. (c) Hence show that $$A,B,C,D$$ all lie on the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Compute side lengths, apply Pythagoras; circumcentre is midpoint of hypotenuse for right triangles.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$A(-1,9),~B(6,10),~C(7,3),~D(0,2)$$ lie on a circle. (a) Show $$ABCD$$ is a square. (b) Find its area. (c) Find the centre of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Show sides equal and perpendicular using vectors; centre is midpoint of diagonal.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$\overrightarrow{AB}=(7,1),~\overrightarrow{BC}=(1,-7),$$ with $$|\overrightarrow{AB}|^2=|\overrightarrow{BC}|^2=50,$$ and $$\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{BC}=7(1)+1(-7)=0$$ ⇒ sides equal and perpendicular ⇒ square. (b) Area $$=\text{side}^2=50.$$ (c) Centre = midpoint of diagonal $$A,C$$: $$\Big(\frac{-1+7}{2},\frac{9+3}{2}\Big)=(3,6).$$ Radius $$r=\sqrt{50}/2=5.$$ Hence circle $$\boxed{(x-3)^2+(y-6)^2=25}. $$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$D(-12,-3),~E(-10,b),~F(2,-5)$$ lie on a circle with $$\angle DEF=90^\circ$$ and $$b>0$$. (a) Find $$b$$. (b) Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: For perpendicular lines: $$m_{DE}\cdot m_{EF}=-1$$; a right angle subtends a diameter ⇒ centre is midpoint of diameter $$DF$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$m_{DE}=\frac{b+3}{2},~m_{EF}=\frac{-5-b}{12},~m_{DE}m_{EF}=-1\Rightarrow-\frac{(b+3)(b+5)}{24}=-1\Rightarrow b^2+8b-9=0.$$ So $$b=\frac{-8\pm\sqrt{100}}{2}=1,-9$$ and since $$b>0\Rightarrow\boxed{b=1}.$$ (b) Right angle at $$E$$ ⇒ diameter is $$DF$$. Centre $$O=\Big(\frac{-12+2}{2},\frac{-3+(-5)}{2}\Big)=(-5,-4).$$ Radius squared $$r^2=OD^2=(7)^2+(-1)^2=50.$$ Hence $$\boxed{(x+5)^2+(y+4)^2=50}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has equation $$x^2+2x+y^2-24y-24=0.$$ (a) Find the centre and radius of the circle. (b) The points $$A(-13,17)$$ and $$B(11,7)$$ lie on the circumference. Show that $$AB$$ is a diameter. (c) The point $$C$$ lies on the negative x-axis and the angle $$ACB=90^\circ$$. Find the coordinates of $$C$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Complete the square to find the centre and radius; check that A,B satisfy the circle and midpoint equals centre. Use circle geometry (right angle in semicircle).
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Rewrite: $$(x^2+2x+1)+(y^2-24y+144)=24+1+144\Rightarrow(x+1)^2+(y-12)^2=169.$$ Hence centre $$(-1,12)$$ and radius $$13$$. (b) Midpoint of $$A,B$$ is $$\Big(\frac{-13+11}{2},\frac{17+7}{2}\Big)=(-1,12),$$ equal to centre ⇒ $$AB$$ is a diameter. (c) Right angle on semicircle ⇒ $$C$$ lies on circle and $$\angle ACB=90^\circ$$ ⇒ x-axis (y=0). Substitute $$y=0$$ in circle: $$(x+1)^2+(0-12)^2=169\Rightarrow x^2+2x+1+144=169\Rightarrow x^2+2x-24=0\Rightarrow(x+6)(x-4)=0,$$ so $$x=-6$$ or $$x=4$$. Negative x-axis ⇒ $$\boxed{C(-6,0)}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line segment $$QR$$ is a diameter of the circle with centre $$C$$, where $$Q(11,12),~R(-5,0)$$. The point $$P(13,6)$$ lies on the circle. (a) Find $$C$$. (b) Find the radius. (c) Write the equation of the circle. (d) Show that $$P$$ lies on the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use midpoint formula for centre and distance for radius. Verify by substitution.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: Show that $$(0,0)$$ lies inside the circle $$(x-5)^2+(y+2)^2=30.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$r^2=30,$$ while $$OC^2=(5)^2+(-2)^2=25+4=29<30.$$ Thus origin is **inside** the circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has equation $$x^2+3x+y^2+6y=3x-2y-7.$$ (a) Find the centre and radius of the circle. (b) Find the points where it meets the y-axis. (c) Show that it does not intersect the x-axis.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Rearrange to standard form and complete the square for centre and radius. Substitute to find intercepts.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Simplify: $$x^2+3x+y^2+6y=3x-2y-7\Rightarrow x^2+y^2+8y+2y+7=0$$ Wait, combine correctly: $$x^2+3x-3x+y^2+6y+2y+7=0\Rightarrow x^2+y^2+8y+7=0.$$ Completing square: $$(y^2+8y+16)=(x^2+7+16)\Rightarrow(x^2)+(y+4)^2=9.$$ Hence centre $$(0,-4)$$ and radius $$r=3.$$ (b) For y-axis, x=0: $$(y+4)^2=9\Rightarrow y=-1,-7.$$ So intercepts (0,-1) and (0,-7). (c) For x-axis, y=0: $$x^2+(4)^2=9\Rightarrow x^2= -7,$$ impossible ⇒ no real intersection ⇒ doesn’t meet x-axis.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The centres of circles $$(x-8)^2+(y-8)^2=117$$ and $$(x+1)^2+(y-3)^2=106$$ are $$P(8,8)$$ and $$Q(-1,3)$$ respectively. (a) Show that $$P$$ lies on the circle $$(x+1)^2+(y-3)^2=106$$. (b) Find the length of $$PQ$$.

The points $$A(-1,0),~B\Big(\frac{1}{2},\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\Big),~C\Big(\frac{1}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\Big)$$ are vertices of a triangle. (a) Show that the circle $$x^2+y^2=1$$ passes through these points. (b) Show that $$\triangle ABC$$ is equilateral.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Substitute coordinates and compare distances between points.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Substitution gives $$(-1)^2+0^2=1,~(\tfrac12)^2+(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2})^2=\tfrac14+\tfrac34=1,$$ so all lie on $$x^2+y^2=1$$. (b) $$AB^2=\left(\frac12+1\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}-0\right)^2=\left(\frac32\right)^2+\frac{3}{4}=\frac{9+3}{4}=3,$$ $$BC^2=(0)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}-(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2})\right)^2=(\sqrt3)^2=3,$$ $$CA^2=\left(-1-\frac12\right)^2+\left(0-(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2})\right)^2=\left(-\frac32\right)^2+\frac{3}{4}=\frac{12}{4}=3.$$ Hence all sides equal ⇒ equilateral.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: A circle with equation $$(x-k)^2+(y-3k)^2=13$$ passes through the point $$(3,0).$$ (a) Find the two possible values of $$k$$. (b) Given that $$k>0,$$ write down the equation of the circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle, centre $$(p,q)$$, radius $$25$$, meets the x-axis at $$(-7,0)$$ and $$(7,0)$$, where $$q>0$$. (a) Find the values of $$p$$ and $$q$$. (b) Find the coordinates of the points where the circle meets the y-axis.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: The x-intercepts are symmetric about the centre, so $$p$$ is midpoint of $$x$$-coordinates, and $$q$$ found using $$r^2=(x-p)^2+(y-q)^2$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Midpoint of x-intercepts: $$p=\frac{-7+7}{2}=0.$$ Radius 25 ⇒ $$r^2=(7-0)^2+(0-q)^2=49+q^2=625\Rightarrow q^2=576\Rightarrow q=24$$ (since $$q>0$$). (b) Equation of circle: $$x^2+(y-24)^2=625.$$ On y-axis, $$x=0\Rightarrow(y-24)^2=625\Rightarrow y-24=\pm25\Rightarrow y=49,-1.$$ Hence intersections: $$(0,49)$$ and $$(0,-1).$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The point $$A(-3,-7)$$ lies on the circle centre $$(5,1)$$. Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at $$A$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: The radius $$CA$$ is perpendicular to tangent at $$A$$. Find radius slope, then negative reciprocal for tangent.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Centre $$(5,1),~A(-3,-7)\Rightarrow m_{CA}=\frac{1-(-7)}{5-(-3)}=\frac{8}{8}=1\Rightarrow m_T=-1.$$ Using point-slope form: $$y+7=-1(x+3)\Rightarrow y=-x-10.$$ Hence tangent $$\boxed{x+y+10=0}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line segment $$AB$$ is a chord of a circle centre $$(2,-1)$$, where $$A(3,7)$$ and $$B(-5,3)$$. The line $$AC$$ is a diameter of the circle. Find the area of $$\triangle ABC$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: The diameter passes through the centre ⇒ slope of $$AC$$ = slope of $$CB$$ perpendicular to it; area by determinant formula.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Using determinant formula for triangle area: $$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}|x_1(y_2-y_3)+x_2(y_3-y_1)+x_3(y_1-y_2)|.$$ First find $$C$$ by using diameter rule: midpoint of $$AC=(2,-1)$$ ⇒ $$\Big(\frac{3+x_C}{2},\frac{7+y_C}{2}\Big)=(2,-1)\Rightarrow3+x_C=4,~7+y_C=-2\Rightarrow x_C=1,~y_C=-9.$$ Hence $$C(1,-9).$$ Now area $$=\frac{1}{2}|3(7-3)+(-5)(3-(-9))+1((-9)-7)|=\frac{1}{2}|12+(-5)(12)+1(-16)|=\frac{1}{2}|12-60-16|=\frac{1}{2}\times64=32.$$ Thus area $$\boxed{32\text{ units}^2.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$C$$ has equation $$(x-6)^2+(y-5)^2=17.$$ The lines $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$ are each tangent to the circle and intersect at the point $$(0,12)$$. Find the equations of $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$, giving your answers in the form $$y=mx+c.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Tangent from point $$(x_1,y_1)$$ to $$(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2$$ satisfies $$(x_1-h)(x-h)+(y_1-k)(y-k)=r^2.$$ Substituting $$(x_1,y_1)=(0,12),~(h,k)=(6,5),~r^2=17$$ gives the tangent equations.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: From formula: $$(0-6)(x-6)+(12-5)(y-5)=17\Rightarrow-6(x-6)+7(y-5)=17\Rightarrow-6x+36+7y-35=17\Rightarrow6x-7y+16=0.$$ For second tangent, general line through $(0,12)$ is $y=mx+12$. Substitute in circle: $$(x-6)^2+(mx+12-5)^2=17\Rightarrow(1+m^2)x^2+2x(7m-6)+(85+36m+m^2)=0.$$ Discriminant=0 ⇒ $$b^2-4ac=0\Rightarrow(7m-6)^2-4(1+m^2)(85+36m+m^2)=0$$ Simplify ⇒ quadratic in $$m$$ ⇒ $$m_1=-\frac{4}{3},~m_2=\frac{3}{4}.$$ Hence $$l_1: y=-\frac{4}{3}x+12,~l_2: y=\frac{3}{4}x+12.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$A(3,7)$$ and $$B(5,1)$$ lie on a circle with centre $$C$$. (a) Find the equation of the line through midpoint $$M$$ of $$AB$$ and centre $$C$$. (b) Given the x-coordinate of $$C$$ is $$-2$$, find the equation of the circle. (c) Find the area of $$\triangle ABC.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find midpoint, slope of $$AB$$, find perpendicular slope, and use known x-coordinate for $$C$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) $$M=\Big(\frac{3+5}{2},\frac{7+1}{2}\Big)=(4,4),~m_{AB}=\frac{1-7}{5-3}=-3\Rightarrow m_\perp=\frac{1}{3}.$$ Equation of line through $$M(4,4): y-4=\frac{1}{3}(x-4)\Rightarrow x-3y+8=0.$$ (b) Centre $$C$$ lies on this line with $$x=-2$$ ⇒ $$-2-3y+8=0\Rightarrow y=2.$$ Hence $$C(-2,2).$$ Radius squared $$r^2=(3+2)^2+(7-2)^2=25+25=50.$$ Equation: $$\boxed{(x+2)^2+(y-2)^2=50.}$$ (c) Area by determinant formula: $$\frac{1}{2}|3(1-2)+5(2-7)+(-2)(7-1)|=\frac{1}{2}|3(-1)+5(-5)+(-2)(6)|=\frac{1}{2}|-3-25-12|=\frac{1}{2}\times40=20.$$ So area $$\boxed{20\text{ units}^2.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$C$$ has equation $$(x-3)^2+(y+3)^2=52.$$ The baselines $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$ are tangents to the circle and have gradient $$\frac{4}{3}$$. (a) Find the points of intersection $$P,Q$$ of the tangents and the circle. (b) Find the equations of $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$, giving your answers in the form $$ax+by+c=0.$$
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use line form $$y=mx+c$$, substitute in circle, and use discriminant $$=0$$ to find possible $$c$$ values (tangent condition).

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$C$$ has equation $$x^2+6x+y^2-2y=7.$$ The lines $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$ are tangents to the circle meeting at the point $$(10,6).$$ Find (a) the equations of $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$, (b) the points of intersection $$P,Q$$ of the tangents with the circle, (c) the area of quadrilateral $$APRQ$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find circle’s centre and radius by completing square, use tangent condition (discriminant = 0) to find slopes.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Complete the square: $$(x+3)^2+(y-1)^2=17,$$ centre $(-3,1)$, radius $\sqrt{17}$. Tangent form $y-6=m(x-10)$, substitute in circle, discriminant = 0: $$(x+3)^2+[m(x-10)+5]^2=17.$$ Expand and solve ⇒ quadratic in $x$: $$(1+m^2)x^2+2x[3+m(5-10m)] +[...] = 0.$$ Discriminant $=0$ ⇒ $$m^2+10m-3=0$$ ⇒ $$m_1=-5+2\sqrt{7},~m_2=-5-2\sqrt{7}.$$ (b) Substitute each $m$ into line equation to find $P,Q$. (c) Use coordinate geometry area formula for quadrilateral.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle $$C$$ has centre $$(6,9)$$ and radius $$\sqrt{50}.$$ The line $$l$$ with equation $$x+y-21=0$$ intersects the circle at the points $$P,Q$$. (a) Find the coordinates of $$P$$ and $$Q$$. (b) Find equations of the tangents $$l_1$$ and $$l_2$$ at $$P,Q$$ respectively. (c) Find the equation of the line perpendicular bisector of chord $$PQ$$. (d) Show that the two tangents and the perpendicular bisector intersect at one point $$R$$, and find $$R$$. (e) Calculate the area of the kite $$APRQ$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Substitute $$y=21-x$$ into circle and solve; find tangent slopes from radii, then bisector and intersection.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Sub: $$(x-6)^2+(21-x-9)^2=50\Rightarrow(x-6)^2+(12-x)^2=50\Rightarrow2x^2-36x+180=50\Rightarrow2x^2-36x+130=0\Rightarrow x^2-18x+65=0.$$ Roots $$x=13,5$$ ⇒ $$P(13,8),~Q(5,16).$$ (b) Radii slopes: $$m_P=\frac{8-9}{13-6}=-\frac{1}{7}\Rightarrow m_{t1}=7,$$ $$m_Q=\frac{16-9}{5-6}=-7\Rightarrow m_{t2}=\frac{1}{7}.$$ Tangents: $$l_1: y-8=7(x-13)\Rightarrow7x-y-83=0,$$ $$l_2: y-16=\frac{1}{7}(x-5)\Rightarrow x-7y+107=0.$$ (c) Midpoint of $$PQ(9,12)$$, slope $$m_{PQ}=\frac{16-8}{5-13}=-1\Rightarrow m_\perp=1$$ ⇒ $$y-12=x-9\Rightarrow x-y+3=0.$$ (d) Solve $$7x-y-83=0,~x-y+3=0$$ ⇒ $$x=12.57,~y=15.57$$ ⇒ $$R(12.57,15.57).$$ All three intersect at $$R$$. (e) Use kite area formula with diagonals.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line $$y=-3x+12$$ meets the coordinate axes at $$A$$ and $$B$$. The line segment $$AB$$ is a diameter of a circle. Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Find intercepts, midpoint, and radius from half the diagonal.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Intercepts: at x-axis (y=0): $$x=4\Rightarrow A(4,0)$$; at y-axis (x=0): $$y=12\Rightarrow B(0,12).$$ Centre = midpoint $$O(2,6),$$ radius $$r^2=(4-2)^2+(0-6)^2=4+36=40.$$ Equation: $$\boxed{(x-2)^2+(y-6)^2=40.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$A(-3,-2),~B(-6,0),~C(1,9)$$ lie on the circumference of a circle such that $$\angle ABC=90^\circ.$$ (a) Find the value of $$q$$. (b) Find the equation of the circle.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$R(-4,3),~S(7,4),~T(8,-7)$$ lie on the circumference of a circle. (a) Show that $$RT$$ is the diameter of the circle. (b) Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Check $$RS^2+ST^2=RT^2$$ or midpoint of RT equals circle’s centre.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$A(-4,0),~B(4,8),~C(6,0)$$ lie on the circumference of a circle. Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use perpendicular bisectors of two chords.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: Chord $$AB:~M_{AB}(0,4),~m_{AB}=\frac{8-0}{4-(-4)}=1\Rightarrow m_\perp=-1.$$ ⇒ $$y-4=-1(x-0)\Rightarrow x+y-4=0.$$ Chord $$BC:~M_{BC}(5,4),~m_{BC}=\frac{0-8}{6-4}=-4\Rightarrow m_\perp=\frac{1}{4}.$$ ⇒ $$y-4=\frac{1}{4}(x-5)\Rightarrow x-4y+11=0.$$ Solve: $$x+y-4=0,~x-4y+11=0\Rightarrow y=3,~x=1.$$ So centre $$(1,3).$$ Radius squared $$r^2=(1+4)^2+(3-0)^2=25+9=34.$$ Hence circle $$\boxed{(x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=34.}$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$A(-7,7),\ B(1,9),\ C(3,1),\ D(-7,1)$$ lie on a circle. (a) Find the perpendicular bisector of (i) $$AB$$ (ii) $$CD$$. (b) Hence find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use midpoint–slope for each chord: midpoint $$M=\big(\tfrac{x_1+x_2}{2},\tfrac{y_1+y_2}{2}\big)$$, slope $$m=\tfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}$$, bisector slope $$m_\perp=-\tfrac1m$$ (vertical if segment is horizontal). Centre is intersection of the two bisectors; radius from any given point.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a)(i) $$M_{AB}=\Big(\tfrac{-7+1}{2},\tfrac{7+9}{2}\Big)=(-3,8),\ m_{AB}=\tfrac{9-7}{1-(-7)}=\tfrac14\Rightarrow m_\perp=-4.$$ Line through $$(-3,8):\ y-8=-4(x+3)\Rightarrow \boxed{\,4x+y+4=0\,}.$$ (ii) $$M_{CD}=\Big(\tfrac{3+(-7)}{2},\tfrac{1+1}{2}\Big)=(-2,1),\ m_{CD}=0$$ (horizontal) $$\Rightarrow$$ bisector is vertical: \boxed{$$x=-2$$}. (b) Centre $$O$$ at the intersection: from $$x=-2$$ in $$4x+y+4=0\Rightarrow y=4$$, so $$O(-2,4).$$ Radius squared from $$A$$: $$r^2=(\!-2+7)^2+(4-7)^2=5^2+(-3)^2=34.$$ Hence the circle is \boxed{$$(x+2)^2+(y-4)^2=34$$}.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Common chord, intersection points & kite area
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circles $$(x-5)^2+(y-3)^2=20$$ (centre $$A(5,3)$$) and $$(x-10)^2+(y-8)^2=10$$ (centre $$B(10,8)$$) meet at $$P,Q$$. (a) Find the equation of line $$PQ$$ in the form $$ax+by+c=0$$. (b) Find the coordinates of $$P$$ and $$Q$$. (c) Find the area of the kite $$APBQ$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: (a) The common chord is the **radical axis**: subtract circle equations to eliminate $$x^2+y^2$$. (b) Solve the line with one circle. (c) For two intersecting circles, $$PQ\perp AB$$; area of kite $$=\tfrac12\cdot |AB|\cdot|PQ|$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: (a) Expand and tidy: first gives $$x^2+y^2-10x-6y+14=0,$$ second $$x^2+y^2-20x-16y+154=0.$$ Subtract ⇒ \boxed{$$x+y-14=0$$}. (b) Put $$y=14-x$$ in first circle: $$(x-5)^2+(11-x)^2=20\Rightarrow2x^2-32x+126=0\Rightarrow x^2-16x+63=0\Rightarrow x=7,9.$$ Thus \boxed{$$P(7,7),\ Q(9,5)$$}. (c) $$|AB|=\sqrt{(10-5)^2+(8-3)^2}=\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt2,$$ $$|PQ|=\sqrt{(9-7)^2+(5-7)^2}=\sqrt8=2\sqrt2.$$ Hence area $$=\tfrac12(5\sqrt2)(2\sqrt2)=\tfrac12\cdot20=\boxed{10}.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circle has centre $$C(5,-1)$$ and passes through $$A(1,3)$$. (a) Find the equation of the tangent at $$A$$. (b) A line parallel to this tangent passes through the midpoint of $$CA$$ and meets the circle at $$B,D$$. Find $$BD$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Tangent ⟂ radius; midpoint line parallel; chord length via distance.
Chapter 6-Circles.solution_text: $$(a)\ m_{CA}=\frac{4}{-4}=-1\Rightarrow m_{\tan}=1.$$ $$y-3=x-1.$$ $$(b)\ M(3,1).$$ Distance from centre to parallel line $$=\sqrt8.$$ $$r^2=32.$$ $$BD=2\sqrt{32-8}=4\sqrt6.$$

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Line cuts circle with fixed area
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The line $$y=mx+k$$ cuts the circle $$x^2+y^2=25$$ forming a segment of constant area $$\frac{25\pi}{4}$$. Find the relation between $$m$$ and $$k$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Use area of circular segment; distance from centre fixed.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Circle through intersection of two lines
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The lines $$y=2x+1$$ and $$y=-x+7$$ intersect the circle $$x^2+y^2=20$$ at $$A,B$$ respectively. Find the equation of the circle with diameter $$AB$$.
The chord of the circle $$x^2+y^2=16$$ has equation $$y=mx+4\sqrt{1+m^2}$$. Find the envelope of the family of chords.
The curve $$y=e^x$$ intersects the circle $$x^2+y^2=5$$ at $$A,B$$. Show that the area enclosed is finite and find the limits of integration.
The tangent from $$P(a,0)$$ to the circle $$x^2+y^2=9$$ has length $$6$$. Find $$a$$.
The circle $$x^2+y^2+2ax+4y+1=0$$ cuts the circle $$x^2+y^2=9$$ orthogonally. Find $$a$$.
The tangent at $$Q(4,3)$$ to the circle $$x^2+y^2=25$$ forms a region with the circle. Find the area of the smaller region.
The centre of a circle lies on $$x-y=2$$ and passes through $$A(4,1)$$ and $$B(6,5)$$. Find the equation of the circle.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Intersect perpendicular bisector with given line.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The chord of the circle $$x^2+y^2=25$$ cut by $$y=mx+3$$ has length $$L$$. Find the value of $$m$$ for which $$L$$ is maximum.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Max chord when line passes through centre.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The region bounded by $$x^2+y^2=9$$ and $$y=|x-1|$$ is finite. Find its area.
A point $$P(x,y)$$ moves such that its distance from the circle $$x^2+y^2=4$$ is twice its distance from $$(-2,0)$$. Find the locus.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Distance from point to circle definition.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The tangent and normal at a point on $$x^2+y^2=10$$ meet the y-axis at $$A,B$$. Show that $$AB$$ is constant.
The curves $$y=x^3$$ and $$y=4-x$$ intersect at $$A,B$$. Find the equation of the circle through $$A,B$$ and $$(-1,1)$$.
The common internal tangents of $$x^2+y^2=9$$ and $$(x-10)^2+y^2=1$$ meet at $$P$$. Find the coordinates of $$P$$.
The circles $$x^2+y^2=25$$ and $$(x-6)^2+y^2=25$$ overlap. Find the area of the common region.
The line $$y=mx+c$$ intersects the circle $$x^2+y^2=9$$ at exactly one point. Find the condition on $$m,c$$.
The region bounded by $$x^2+y^2=9$$ and $$y=\ln(x+2)$$ is finite. Find the x-limits.
The tangents from $$A(a,0)$$ to $$x^2+y^2=9$$ form a triangle with the axes. Find $$a$$ for minimum area.
The midpoint of a chord of $$x^2+y^2=16$$ lies on $$y=2x$$. Find the locus of the chord.
Show that the locus of the intersection of tangents at the endpoints of a variable chord of $$x^2+y^2=a^2$$ is the circle itself.
The line $$y=mx+1$$ cuts the circle $$x^2+y^2=25$$ in a chord $$AB$$. (a) Show the midpoint of $$AB$$ lies on a fixed line. (b) Find that line.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Chord midpoint lies on perpendicular from centre to chord.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The points $$A(-5,0),~B(5,0)$$ are fixed. A point $$P$$ moves on the circle $$x^2+y^2=25$$. Find the maximum area of $$\triangle ABP$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Base fixed; height maximised when perpendicular distance is max.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The curve $$y=\frac{1}{x}$$ intersects the circle $$x^2+y^2=5$$ at $$A,B$$. (a) Show intersections exist. (b) Find the area enclosed.
The chord of the circle $$x^2+y^2=13$$ passes through $$P(2,3)$$. Find the equation of the chord of maximum length.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Longest chord through a point passes through centre.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The tangents from $$P(a,0)$$ to the circle $$x^2+y^2=9$$ make an angle of $$60^\circ$$. Find $$arianTheorem (just give answer)$$
The curve $$y=x^3$$ cuts the circle $$x^2+y^2=10$$ at $$A,B$$. Show the region enclosed is finite and find its area.
The tangent to $$x^2+y^2=9$$ at point $$P$$ meets the x-axis at $$T$$. Find the locus of $$T$$.
Chapter 6-Circles.hint: Equation of tangent at general point.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The circles $$x^2+y^2=13,$$ $$(x-4)^2+y^2=13,$$ $$(x-2)^2+(y-4)^2=13$$ intersect. Find the common point of their radical axes.
The chords of $$x^2+y^2=25$$ with equations $$y=mx\pm4$$ are parallel. Find the distance between them.

Chapter 6-Circles.question_title: Area bounded by circle and line
Chapter 6-Circles.question_text: The region bounded by $$x^2+y^2=16$$ and $$y=2$$ is shaded. Find its area.
Find the equation of the circle orthogonal to $$x^2+y^2=25$$ and passing through $$(3,4)$$.
The chord of $$x^2+y^2=25$$ cut by $$y=mx+3$$ has length $$8$$. Find $$m$$.
The tangent to $$x^2+y^2=10$$ at $$P$$ meets $$y=x^2$$ at $$Q$$. Find the locus of $$Q$$.
The point $$P(x,y)$$ lies on $$x^2+y^2=25$$. Find the maximum value of $$x+y$$.
The curve $$y=\arctan x$$ intersects $$x^2+y^2=4$$. Show the enclosed area is finite.
The common chord of $$x^2+y^2=9$$ and $$(x-2)^2+y^2=9$$ moves. Find its locus.
The tangents from $$A(7,0)$$ to $$x^2+y^2=9$$ form triangle $$APQ$$. Find the centroid.
The point $$P$$ moves so that its distance from $$(-3,0)$$ equals its distance from the circle $$x^2+y^2=1$$. Find the locus.
The points $$A,B$$ on $$x^2+y^2=16$$ subtend angle $$60^\circ$$ at the centre. Find the area between arc $$AB$$ and chord $$AB$$.
The line $$y=mx+c$$ cuts $$x^2+y^2=16$$ in a chord of minimum length. Find the condition on $$m,c$$.
